fields.name: AHB_DMA_PL1
fields.text: Bus arbitration priority of the RFPT master, from 0 (lowest) to 15 (highest).

fields.name: AHB_DMA_PL2
fields.text: Bus arbitration priority of the LCD master, from 0 (lowest) to 15 (highest).

fields.name: AHB_DMA_PL3
fields.text: Bus arbitration priority of the GEN-DMA master, from 0 (lowest) to 15 (highest).

fields.name: AHB_DMA_PL4
fields.text: Bus arbitration priority of the CRYPTO-DMA master, from 0 (lowest) to 15 (highest).

fields.name: AHB_DMA_DFLT_MASTER
fields.text: ID of the master the bus grants when no master asks for it. Codes: 0 = a dummy master; 1 = RFPT; 2 = LCD; 3 = GEN-DMA; also 3 = CRYPTO-DMA.

fields.name: AHB_DMA_WTEN
fields.text: Turns on the weighted-token arbitration scheme.

fields.name: AHB_DMA_TCL
fields.text: Length of one arbitration period in clock cycles (tokens); the master counters reload at the start of each period. Suggested: all the AHB_DMA_CCLMx_REG values added up, plus 2 tokens per master, that is plus 6.

fields.name: AHB_DMA_CCLM
fields.text: Tokens (AHB clock cycles) a master may spend on the bus before it must arbitrate against a lower-priority master that still holds tokens. Masters with tokens left win over masters that have spent theirs. The token settings together must not exceed the total allotted. Zero gives the master unlimited tokens, so it always arbitrates in the upper tier.

fields.name: AHB_DMA_CCLM
fields.text: Token count for master 2, working as AHB_DMA_CCLM1_REG does.

fields.name: AHB_DMA_CCLM
fields.text: Token count for master 3, working as AHB_DMA_CCLM1_REG does.

fields.name: AHB_DMA_CCLM
fields.text: Token count for master 4, working as AHB_DMA_CCLM1_REG does.

fields.name: AHB_DMA_VERSION
fields.text: AHB DMA version.

fields.name: LCDC_MODE_EN
fields.text: Turns the LCD controller mode on (1) or off (0).

fields.name: LCDC_VSYNC_POL
fields.text: VSYNC polarity: 0 positive, 1 negative.

fields.name: LCDC_HSYNC_POL
fields.text: HSYNC polarity: 0 positive, 1 negative.

fields.name: LCDC_DE_POL
fields.text: DE polarity: 0 positive, 1 negative.

fields.name: LCDC_VSYNC_SCPL
fields.text: When 1, VSYNC is asserted for one cycle on each line; 0 turns this off.

fields.name: LCDC_PIXCLKOUT_POL
fields.text: Polarity of the output pixel clock: 0 positive, 1 negative.

fields.name: LCDC_FORCE_BLANK
fields.text: When 1, the output is held blank; 0 turns this off.

fields.name: LCDC_SFRAME_UPD
fields.text: When 1, a single frame is updated; 0 turns this off.

fields.name: LCDC_PIXCLKOUT_SEL
fields.text: Source of the display's output pixel clock: 0 derived from the pixel pipeline clock, 1 from the format pipeline clock; LCDC_CLKCTRL_REG is related.

fields.name: LCDC_OUT_MODE
fields.text: Output mode: 0000 parallel RGB, 1000 JDI MIP; every other code is reserved.

fields.name: LCDC_MIPI_OFF
fields.text: MIPI off, the SPI mode of the MIPI standard: 0 disabled, 1 enabled.

fields.name: LCDC_FORM_OFF
fields.text: Formatting off: 0 disabled, 1 enabled.

fields.name: LCDC_DSCAN
fields.text: Double horizontal scan: 0 disabled, 1 enabled.

fields.name: LCDC_TMODE
fields.text: Test mode: 0 disabled, 1 enabled.

fields.name: LCDC_SEC_CLK_DIV
fields.text: Divider from the LCD controller's main clock to the format pipeline clock; the result has a period of (LCDC_SEC_CLK_DIV + 1) main-clock periods.

fields.name: LCDC_DMA_HOLD
fields.text: Time held before the DMA starts.

fields.name: LCDC_CLK_DIV
fields.text: Divider from the format pipeline clock (set by LCDC_SEC_CLK_DIV) to the pixel pipeline clock; the result has a period of LCDC_CLK_DIV format-clock periods, and 0 divides by one.

fields.name: LCDC_BG_RED
fields.text: Red part of the background colour.

fields.name: LCDC_BG_GREEN
fields.text: Green part of the background colour.

fields.name: LCDC_BG_BLUE
fields.text: Blue part of the background colour.

fields.name: LCDC_BG_ALPHA
fields.text: Alpha part of the background colour.

fields.name: LCDC_RES_X
fields.text: Horizontal resolution, in pixels.

fields.name: LCDC_RES_Y
fields.text: Vertical resolution, in pixels.

fields.name: LCDC_FPORCH_X
fields.text: Horizontal front porch, in lines.

fields.name: LCDC_FPORCH_Y
fields.text: Vertical front porch, in pixel clocks.

fields.name: LCDC_BLANKING_X
fields.text: Horizontal blanking period, in VSYNC lines.

fields.name: LCDC_BLANKING_Y
fields.text: Vertical blanking period, the HSYNC pulse length.

fields.name: LCDC_BPORCH_X
fields.text: Horizontal back porch, in lines.

fields.name: LCDC_BPORCH_Y
fields.text: Vertical back porch, in pixel clocks.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_TE_DIS
fields.text: Stops sampling of the tearing-effect signal from the LCD device: 0 the signal is sampled, 1 it is not.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_CSX_FORCE
fields.text: When 1, DBIB CSX is driven to the value in LCDC_DBIB_CSX_FORCE_VAL; 0 leaves it unforced.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_CSX_FORCE_VAL
fields.text: Level DBIB CSX is forced to while LCDC_DBIB_CSX_FORCE is set; it also sets the active level of CSX when LCDC_DBIB_CSX_FORCE is clear.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_SPI_PAD
fields.text: Data padding: 0 off, 1 on.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_RESX
fields.text: DBIB RESX, the reset line of a MIPI DBIB display.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_DMA_EN
fields.text: When 1, pixels from the DMA are sent to the DBIB display; 0 turns this off.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_SPI3_EN
fields.text: Turns the SPI3 interface on (1) or off (0).

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_SPI4_EN
fields.text: Turns the SPI4 interface on (1) or off (0).

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_SPI_CPHA
fields.text: Data phase of the SPI interface.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_SPI_CPOL
fields.text: Polarity of the SPI clock (SCL).

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_SPI_JDI
fields.text: When 1, line addresses are inserted between horizontal lines, the JDI SPI output format; 0 turns this off.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_SPI_HOLD
fields.text: When 1, command HOLD operation is used, binding command and data transfers together; 0 turns it off.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_SPI_INV_ADDR
fields.text: When 1, horizontal line addresses are inverted; 0 turns this off.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_INV_DATA
fields.text: Data inversion: 0 off, 1 on.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_JDI_INV_PIX
fields.text: Bit order on the JDI parallel interface: 0 MSB to LSB, 1 LSB to MSB.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_JDI_SOFT_RST
fields.text: Soft reset of the JDI timing generation: 0 off, 1 on.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_FMT
fields.text: Output format; the codes depend on the output interface. For SPI3/SPI4: 0x06 RGB111-1, two zero bits then one bit each of R, G, B for pixel n and again for pixel n+1; 0x07 RGB111-2, R, G, B of pixel n and a zero bit, then the same for pixel n+1; 0x08 RGB111-3, the R, G, B bits of successive pixels packed back to back; 0x09 RGB111-4, D(n), D(n+1), D(n+2) and on back to back; 0x10 RGB332; 0x11 RGB444; 0x12 RGB565; 0x13 RGB666; 0x14 RGB888. For the JDI parallel interface: 0x0A RGB222.

fields.name: LCDC_TE_INV
fields.text: Inverts the TE (tearing effect) signal: 0 not inverted, 1 inverted.

fields.name: LCDC_PARIF_SEL
fields.text: Which parallel interface reaches the GPIO pins: 0 the JDI interface signals, 1 the classic parallel interface.

fields.name: LCDC_L0_EN
fields.text: Turns layer 0 on (1) or off (0).

fields.name: LCDC_L0_COLOUR_MODE
fields.text: Layer 0 colour format: 00001 16-bit RGBX5551, 00010 32-bit RGBX8888, 00100 8-bit RGB332, 00101 16-bit RGB565, 00110 32-bit XRGB8888, 00111 L8 grayscale/palette, 01000 L1 grayscale/palette, 01001 L4 grayscale/palette, 01101 ABGR8888, 01110 BGRA8888.

fields.name: LCDC_L0_START_X
fields.text: Horizontal start of layer 0, as an offset in pixels.

fields.name: LCDC_L0_START_Y
fields.text: Vertical start of layer 0, as an offset in pixels.

fields.name: LCDC_L0_SIZE_X
fields.text: Width of layer 0, in pixels.

fields.name: LCDC_L0_SIZE_Y
fields.text: Height of layer 0, in pixels.

fields.name: LCDC_L0_FB_ADDR
fields.text: Start address of the layer 0 frame buffer.

fields.name: LCDC_L0_FIFO_THR
fields.text: FIFO level at which the layer DMA starts a burst: 00 half the FIFO (default), 01 2 bursts, 10 4 bursts, 11 8 bursts.

fields.name: LCDC_L0_BURST_LEN
fields.text: Layer DMA burst length: 000 16 beats (default), 001 2 beats, 010 4 beats, 011 8 beats, 100 16 beats.

fields.name: LCDC_L0_STRIDE
fields.text: Layer stride: bytes from the start of one line to the next.

fields.name: LCDC_L0_RES_X
fields.text: Horizontal resolution of layer 0, in pixels.

fields.name: LCDC_L0_RES_Y
fields.text: Vertical resolution of layer 0, in pixels.

fields.name: LCDC_JDI_RES_X
fields.text: Horizontal transfer count; set to half the horizontal resolution in pixels.

fields.name: LCDC_JDI_RES_Y
fields.text: Vertical transfer count; set to twice the vertical resolution in lines.

fields.name: LCDC_JDI_FXBLANKING
fields.text: Horizontal front blanking, in half periods of HCK.

fields.name: LCDC_JDI_BXBLANKING
fields.text: Horizontal back blanking, in half periods of HCK.

fields.name: LCDC_JDI_FYBLANKING
fields.text: Vertical front blanking, in half periods of VCK.

fields.name: LCDC_JDI_BYBLANKING
fields.text: Vertical back blanking, in half periods of VCK.

fields.name: LCDC_JDI_HCK_WIDTH
fields.text: Half period of HCK (both its high and low time) in format pipeline clock cycles; 2 at least.

fields.name: LCDC_JDI_XRST_WIDTH
fields.text: XRST width, in format pipeline clock cycles.

fields.name: LCDC_JDI_VST_DELAY
fields.text: Delay from XRST to VST, in format pipeline clock cycles.

fields.name: LCDC_JDI_VST_WIDTH
fields.text: VST width, in format pipeline clock cycles.

fields.name: LCDC_JDI_VCK_DELAY
fields.text: Delay from XRST to VCK, in format pipeline clock cycles.

fields.name: LCDC_JDI_HST_DELAY
fields.text: Delay from VCK to HST, in format pipeline clock cycles.

fields.name: LCDC_JDI_HST_WIDTH
fields.text: HST width, in format pipeline clock cycles.

fields.name: LCDC_JDI_ENB_START_HLINE
fields.text: Horizontal line on which ENB first goes active.

fields.name: LCDC_JDI_ENB_END_HLINE
fields.text: Horizontal line on which ENB is last active.

fields.name: LCDC_JDI_ENB_START_CLK
fields.text: HCK half periods that pass after a VCK transition before ENB is turned on.

fields.name: LCDC_JDI_ENB_WIDTH_CLK
fields.text: High time of ENB, in HCK half periods.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_CMD_SEND
fields.text: Sends a command to the DBI interface.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_CMD_STORE
fields.text: Acts only while the LCDC_DBIB_SPI_JDI bit of LCDC_DBIB_CFG_REG is 1: when set, LCDC_DBIB_CMD_VAL is stored in the register holding the Y position.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_CMD_VAL
fields.text: Data sent to the DBI interface.

fields.name: LCDC_ID
fields.text: Identification value.

fields.name: LCDC_IRQ_TRIGGER_SEL
fields.text: IRQ trigger type: 0 level, 1 edge. A level request stays active in the LCDC until it is cleared by a write to LCDC_INTERRUPT_REG; an edge request needs no clearing.

fields.name: LCDC_FRAME_END_IRQ_EN
fields.text: Frame-end interrupt enable: at frame end in continuous mode, at frame end or idle in single mode.

fields.name: LCDC_TE_IRQ_EN
fields.text: Enables the TE interrupt; the LCDC_DBIB_TE_DIS bit of LCDC_DBIB_CFG_REG also bears on it.

fields.name: LCDC_HSYNC_IRQ_EN
fields.text: Enables the HSYNC interrupt.

fields.name: LCDC_VSYNC_IRQ_EN
fields.text: Enables the VSYNC or TE interrupt; for TE, the LCDC_DBIB_TE_DIS bit of LCDC_DBIB_CFG_REG also bears on it.

fields.name: LCDC_JDI_TIM_SW_RST
fields.text: JDI timing generator soft reset, high while active.

fields.name: LCDC_FRAME_START
fields.text: Frame start, high while active.

fields.name: LCDC_FRAME_END
fields.text: Frame end, high while active.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_CMD_PENDING
fields.text: Reads 1 while a command transfer is under way, 0 when idle.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_CMD_FIFO_FULL
fields.text: Reads 1 when the command FIFO is full, 0 when it is not.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_CMD_FIFO_EMPTY_N
fields.text: Active-low command FIFO empty flag: 0 the FIFO is empty, 1 it holds data.

fields.name: LCDC_DBIB_TE
fields.text: The DBIB tearing effect signal.

fields.name: LCDC_STICKY_UNDERFLOW
fields.text: Latched underflow flag: 0 no underflow, 1 an underflow was seen; it stays 1 until a write to LCDC_INTERRUPT_REG clears it.

fields.name: LCDC_UNDERFLOW
fields.text: Underflow on the transfer now under way: 0 none, 1 detected.

fields.name: LCDC_LAST_ROW
fields.text: The last row is on the display now.

fields.name: LCDC_STAT_CSYNC
fields.text: Level of CSYNC.

fields.name: LCDC_STAT_VSYNC
fields.text: Level of VSYNC.

fields.name: LCDC_STAT_HSYNC
fields.text: Level of HSYNC.

fields.name: LCDC_FRAMEGEN_BUSY
fields.text: High while the frame generator is busy.

fields.name: LCDC_STAT_ACTIVE
fields.text: Active, meaning not in vertical blanking.

fields.name: LCDC_CRC
fields.text: CRC check value.

fields.name: LCDC_L0_DMA_PREFETCH
fields.text: Layer 0 DMA FIFO prefetch level, 0 to 4: 0x0 prefetch off, 0x1 at least 44 bytes, 0x2 at least 84 bytes, 0x3 at least 116 bytes, 0x4 at least 108 bytes; other codes are reserved.

fields.name: LCDC_L0_OFFSETX
fields.text: Negative X offset of the starting pixel, in the range n-1 to 0 where n is pixels / 8.

fields.name: SMP_IDX
fields.text: Index of the bin being sampled now, 0 to 15; compare it with IRQ_IDX before and/or after the ISR changes HALF_PERIOD.

fields.name: IRQ_SCP_EVENT_EN
fields.text: Enables the SCP event interrupt.

fields.name: IRQ_ADC_EN
fields.text: Enables the ADC interrupt.

fields.name: IRQ_CTRL_EN
fields.text: Enables the controller interrupt.

fields.name: IRQ_IDX
fields.text: Sample index, 0 to 15, at which an IRQ fires. Below 8 an IRQ fires in both half cycles (at IRQ_IDX and IRQ_IDX+8); from 8 up only in the second half cycle.

fields.name: IRQ_DIV
fields.text: IRQ divider: LRA/ERM periods between IRQs. 0 and 1 give an IRQ every (half) cycle as IRQ_IDX sets; 2 gives one every second cycle, at the end of the first or both half cycles as IRQ_IDX sets; and so on.

fields.name: SMP_SEL
fields.text: Which signal is stored as samples for the resonance control algorithm: 0 the down-sampled sense voltage, 1 the error voltage (down-sampled sense voltage minus VREF), 2 the duty-cycle signal after the loop filter, 3 the duty-cycle signal after DREF is added.

fields.name: PULLDOWN_EN
fields.text: Enables pull-downs on the LXP and LXN nodes while SC_EVENT=0 and LOOP_EN=0.

fields.name: LOOP_EN
fields.text: Turns the control loop on.

fields.name: LDO_EN
fields.text: Enables the LRA LDO.

fields.name: ADC_EN
fields.text: Enables the LRA ADC.

fields.name: HBRIDGE_EN
fields.text: Enables the H-bridge.

fields.name: LRA_EN
fields.text: Enables the LRA controller.

fields.name: HALF_PERIOD
fields.text: Half the LRA period in steps of 4 μs, which is 125 kHz over the LRA's resonant frequency.

fields.name: AUTO_MODE
fields.text: Automatic frequency control: 0 off, 1 on (not implemented yet).

fields.name: SMP_MODE
fields.text: How data for automatic resonance control is sampled: 0 averages, 1 takes the last sample.

fields.name: POLARITY
fields.text: Square wave polarity: 0 normal, 1 inverted; used to stop quickly.

fields.name: FLT_IN_SEL
fields.text: Filter input source: 0 normal operation, 1 the ADC output is replaced by MAN_FLT_IN.

fields.name: PWM_MODE
fields.text: Where the PWM pulse sits in its period: 0 middle, 1 left, 2 right, 3 alternating.

fields.name: VREF
fields.text: Voltage reference for the haptic driver, signed 16-bit with 7 integer and 8 fraction bits (-128 to +127.99), derived from the wanted current IREF through the haptic device. Formula: VREF = IREF×TRIM_GAIN×AGC_GAIN×128/2.4. IREF is in amperes; TRIM_GAIN is set in LRA_BRD_HS_REG to 6, 8 (the default), 10 or 12; ADC_GAIN, the ADC's normalised gain, is GP_ADC_VALUE×300 mA/[ILRA×128].

fields.name: DREF
fields.text: Duty cycle reference the current loop starts from and settles out of, signed with 7 integer and 8 fraction bits (-128 to +127.99); 5% to 95% (0x0666 to 0x799A) are valid.

fields.name: LRA_SMP_2
fields.text: Sample 2 of the first half cycle, for the resonance control algorithm.

fields.name: LRA_SMP_1
fields.text: Sample 1 of the first half cycle, for the resonance control algorithm.

fields.name: LRA_SMP_4
fields.text: Sample 4 of the first half cycle, for the resonance control algorithm.

fields.name: LRA_SMP_3
fields.text: Sample 3 of the first half cycle, for the resonance control algorithm.

fields.name: LRA_SMP_6
fields.text: Sample 6 of the first half cycle, for the resonance control algorithm.

fields.name: LRA_SMP_5
fields.text: Sample 5 of the first half cycle, for the resonance control algorithm.

fields.name: LRA_SMP_8
fields.text: Sample 8 of the first half cycle, for the resonance control algorithm.

fields.name: LRA_SMP_7
fields.text: Sample 7 of the first half cycle, for the resonance control algorithm.

fields.name: LRA_SMP_10
fields.text: Sample 2 of the second half cycle, for the resonance control algorithm.

fields.name: LRA_SMP_9
fields.text: Sample 1 of the second half cycle, for the resonance control algorithm.

fields.name: LRA_SMP_12
fields.text: Sample 4 of the second half cycle, for the resonance control algorithm.

fields.name: LRA_SMP_11
fields.text: Sample 3 of the second half cycle, for the resonance control algorithm.

fields.name: LRA_SMP_14
fields.text: Sample 6 of the second half cycle, for the resonance control algorithm.

fields.name: LRA_SMP_13
fields.text: Sample 5 of the second half cycle, for the resonance control algorithm.

fields.name: LRA_SMP_16
fields.text: Sample 8 of the second half cycle, for the resonance control algorithm.

fields.name: LRA_SMP_15
fields.text: Sample 7 of the second half cycle, for the resonance control algorithm.

fields.name: FLT_COEF_01
fields.text: Loop filter state-space coefficient a12, signed with 1 integer and 14 fraction bits (-2.000 to +1.999).

fields.name: FLT_COEF_00
fields.text: Loop filter state-space coefficient a11, signed with 1 integer and 14 fraction bits (-2.000 to +1.999).

fields.name: FLT_COEF_10
fields.text: Loop filter state-space coefficient a21, signed with 1 integer and 14 fraction bits (-2.000 to +1.999).

fields.name: FLT_COEF_02
fields.text: Loop filter state-space coefficient b1, signed with 1 integer and 14 fraction bits (-2.000 to +1.999). For the intended loop gain, write b1/ADC_GAIN in place of b1, ADC_GAIN being the ADC's normalised gain, GP_ADC_VALUE×300 mA/[ILRA×128].

fields.name: FLT_COEF_12
fields.text: Loop filter state-space coefficient b2, signed with 1 integer and 14 fraction bits (-2.000 to +1.999). For the intended loop gain, the intended b1 is to be written as b1/ADC_GAIN, ADC_GAIN being the ADC's normalised gain, GP_ADC_VALUE×300 mA/[ILRA×128].

fields.name: FLT_COEF_11
fields.text: Loop filter state-space coefficient a22, signed with 1 integer and 14 fraction bits (-2.000 to +1.999).

fields.name: SCP_LS_TRIM_N
fields.text: Trims the short-circuit protection limit of LSN.

fields.name: SCP_LS_TRIM_P
fields.text: Trims the short-circuit protection limit of LSP.

fields.name: SCP_LS_EN
fields.text: Enables low-side short-circuit protection.

fields.name: ERC_LS_TRIM
fields.text: Low-side edge-rate trim, setting the high-to-low slew: 00 = 25, 01 = 50, 10 = 75, 11 = 100, in MV/s.

fields.name: ERC_LS_EN
fields.text: Enables low-side edge-rate control.

fields.name: TRIM_GAIN
fields.text: Gain of the current-sense amplifier: 0001 x6, 0010 x8, 0100 x10, 1000 x12.

fields.name: HSGND_TRIM
fields.text: High-side ground trim in 0.2 V steps, from 000 = 2.2 V to 111 = 3.6 V; default 100.

fields.name: SCP_HS_TRIM
fields.text: Trims the high-side short-circuit protection limit.

fields.name: SCP_HS_EN
fields.text: Enables high-side short-circuit protection.

fields.name: ERC_HS_TRIM
fields.text: High-side edge-rate trim, setting the low-to-high slew: 00 = 25, 01 = 50, 10 = 75, 11 = 100, in MV/s.

fields.name: ERC_HS_EN
fields.text: Enables high-side edge-rate control.

fields.name: SCP_HS_OUT
fields.text: Output of the high-side short-circuit comparator.

fields.name: SCP_LS_COMP_OUT_N
fields.text: Output of the LSN short-circuit comparator.

fields.name: SCP_LS_COMP_OUT_P
fields.text: Output of the LSP short-circuit comparator.

fields.name: SC_EVENT_LS
fields.text: Low-side short-circuit event flag.

fields.name: SC_EVENT_HS
fields.text: High-side short-circuit event flag.

fields.name: LOOP_STAT
fields.text: Loop saturation flag.

fields.name: LSN_ON
fields.text: Control state of LSN.

fields.name: LSP_ON
fields.text: Control state of LSP.

fields.name: HSN_ON
fields.text: Control state of HSN.

fields.name: HSP_ON
fields.text: Control state of HSP.

fields.name: LSN_STAT
fields.text: Actual gate state of the LSN power FET.

fields.name: LSP_STAT
fields.text: Actual gate state of the LSP power FET.

fields.name: HSN_STAT
fields.text: Actual gate state of the HSN power FET.

fields.name: HSP_STAT
fields.text: Actual gate state of the HSP power FET.

fields.name: LRA_ADC_BUSY
fields.text: ADC conversion state.

fields.name: LRA_ADC_OFFSET
fields.text: ADC offset correction, signed with 3 fraction bits: -16 (0x80) to +15.875 (0x7F) in 0.125 (0x01) steps. ADC gain error has to be corrected inside the VREF calculation.

fields.name: LRA_ADC_TEST_PARAM
fields.text: ADC input selection: 0 or 1 normal, I and Q both on the LRA current-sense voltage; 2 I on the analog test bus at P14 and P15 with Q muted; 3 Q on that test bus with I muted. LRA_ADC_CTRL1_REG[ADC_MUTE] overrides this.

fields.name: LRA_ADC_TEST_IN_SEL
fields.text: Puts the analog test bus on the ADC input.

fields.name: LRA_ADC_FREQ
fields.text: Divider of the ADC clock.

fields.name: LRA_ADC_SIGN
fields.text: Reverses the polarity of the ADC input.

fields.name: LRA_ADC_MUTE
fields.text: 0 normal operation; 1 shorts the ADC inputs together, used for DC offset calibration.

values.text: ADC inputs shorted together, for DC offset calibration.

fields.name: LRA_ADC_START
fields.text: Writing 1 starts an ADC conversion.

fields.name: MAN_FLT_IN
fields.text: Value that stands in for the ADC output when FLT_IN_SEL selects it.

fields.name: GP_ADC_VAL
fields.text: Last conversion result, a signed linear value of 10 to 16 bits. The top 11 bits always hold; the bottom 5 hold only with oversampling, 2 samples giving one extra bit and 32 samples five. For the LRA constant-current or constant-duty loops the plain value reads as signed with 7 integer and 3 fraction bits, -128.000 (0x8000) to +127.875 (0x7FE0) in 0.125 (0x0010) steps; values measured there are always positive.

fields.name: LDO_OK
fields.text: LDO ready flag.

fields.name: LDO_TST
fields.text: Writing 1 connects the LDO output to the test bus through a test switch.

fields.name: LDO_VREF_HOLD
fields.text: LDO reference input handling: 0 tracked, 1 sampled.

fields.name: SPARE
fields.text: Spare bits, unused.

fields.name: SWM_SEL
fields.text: Source of the SWM signal.

fields.name: SWM_MAN
fields.text: Manual SWM level.

fields.name: PWM_SEL
fields.text: Source of the PWM signal.

fields.name: PWM_MAN
fields.text: Manual PWM level.

fields.name: TIMER_TRIM
fields.text: Trims the 20 ns unit delay cell.

fields.name: TIMER_SCALE_TRIM
fields.text: Delay of the MAG and DEMAG signals: 00 60 ns, 01 80 ns, 10 100 ns, 11 120 ns.

fields.name: DFT_SEL
fields.text: Unused.

fields.name: DFT_FORCE_HSPN
fields.text: 1 forces the HSP and HSN power FETs on; 0 leaves them unforced.

fields.name: DFT_EN_TIMER
fields.text: Enables timer trimming.

fields.name: DFT_STALL
fields.text: Holds the state machine in one state: 00 no test, 01 High-Z, 10 Mag, 11 Demag.

fields.name: DFT_CTRL
fields.text: Selects what the test bus connects to.

fields.name: AHB_PRIO

fields.name: AHB2_PRIO

fields.name: AHB_MAX_STALL
fields.text: Most stall cycles the AHB interface may wait, 1 to 15; past that it is raised above high priority. The limit counts per single access, so a following access within a burst can queue for as many cycles again. 0 must not be used: it cannot work and can block the other interfaces.

fields.name: SNC_MAX_STALL

fields.name: CMI_NOT_READY

fields.name: SNC_BASE_ADDRESS

fields.name: OTPC_MODE_PRG_SEL
fields.text: Which arrays of the OTP cell each program request writes in PROG mode: 0x0 normal and redundancy arrays both (the usual case), 0x1 normal array only, 0x2 redundancy array only, 0x3 reserved. It can be changed only in an inactive mode (PDOWN, DSTBY, STBY) and applies from the next time PROG mode is entered.

fields.name: OTPC_MODE_HT_MARG_EN
fields.text: Temperature condition for the margin reads in RINI and PVFY modes: 0 regular, below 85°C; 1 high, 85°C or more. It can be changed only in an inactive mode (PDOWN, DSTBY, STBY), applies from the next PVFY or RINI mode, and has no effect on READ mode.

fields.name: OTPC_MODE_USE_TST_ROW
fields.text: Which area of the OTP cell is used: 0 the main memory area, 1 the test row. Change it only while the controller is inactive (PDOWN, DSTBY, STBY); it acts from the next programming or reading mode.

fields.name: OTPC_MODE_MODE
fields.text: OTPC operating mode: 0x0 PDOWN, OTP supply off; 0x1 DSTBY, deep standby, supply on and internal LDO off; 0x2 STBY, supply and LDO on but memory not selected; 0x3 READ, normal reading; 0x4 PROG, programming; 0x5 PVFY, margin read to verify programming; 0x6 RINI, initial margin read; 0x7 reserved. A change of mode clears OTPC_STAT_REG[OTPC_STAT_MRDY] and makes this field read-only until MRDY returns to 1; the controller must not be used or changed before then.

fields.name: OTPC_STAT_MRDY
fields.text: Mode change status: 0 a change to a new mode is still under way; 1 it is complete, the new mode's function can be used and another mode can be set. It goes to 0 whenever OTPC_MODE_REG[MODE] changes, and the controller must not be used or changed until it is 1.

fields.name: OTPC_STAT_PBUF_EMPTY
fields.text: Programming buffer (PBUF) status: 0 it holds the address and data of a request, and OTPC_PADDR_REG and OTPC_PWORD_REG must not be written; 1 it is empty and a new request can be loaded through those two registers. It goes to 0 each time a write to OTPC_PADDR_REG starts programming in PROG mode.

fields.name: OTPC_STAT_PRDY
fields.text: Programming status: 0 busy, a programming operation is under way; 1 the programming logic is idle.

fields.name: OTPC_PADDR
fields.text: Word address of a programming request; with OTPC_PWORD_REG it forms PBUF, the buffer holding each address and data word to be written into the OTP in PROG mode. Write it after OTPC_PWORD_REG and only while OTPC_STAT_REG[OTPC_STAT_PBUF_EMPTY]=1; it is read-only while that bit is 0. A write to it starts programming when PROG mode is active.

fields.name: OTPC_PWORD
fields.text: Data word of a programming request; with OTPC_PADDR_REG it forms PBUF, the buffer holding each address and data word to be written into the OTP in PROG mode. Write it before OTPC_PADDR_REG and only while OTPC_STAT_REG[OTPC_STAT_PBUF_EMPTY]=1; it is read-only while that bit is 0.

fields.name: OTPC_TIM1_US_T_CSP
fields.text: Time from selecting the OTP memory until it is ready to program, in microseconds less one; 10 μs to 100 μs.

fields.name: OTPC_TIM1_US_T_CS
fields.text: Time from selecting the OTP memory until it is ready for any read, in microseconds less one; 10 μs at least.

fields.name: OTPC_TIM1_US_T_PL
fields.text: Time until the OTP's LDO is on, in microseconds less one; 10 μs at least.

fields.name: OTPC_TIM1_CC_T_RD
fields.text: Count of hclk_c periods for the OTP memory access time, which must exceed 120 ns: 2 × (OTPC_TIM1_CC_T_RD + 1) × hclk period > 120 ns.

fields.name: OTPC_TIM1_CC_T_20NS
fields.text: hclk_c periods, less one, making up more than 20 ns.

fields.name: OTPC_TIM1_CC_T_1US
fields.text: hclk_c periods, less one, making up 1 μs; every microsecond timing in the controller is counted from it.

fields.name: OTPC_TIM2_US_ADD_CC_EN
fields.text: When 1, one extra hclk_c cycle is added to every time interval counted in microseconds; 0 adds none.

fields.name: OTPC_TIM2_US_T_SAS
fields.text: Time after leaving deep standby before an active mode (read or program) can be entered, in microseconds less one; 2 μs at least.

fields.name: OTPC_TIM2_US_T_PPH
fields.text: Time from the last programming pulse until programming mode is turned off in the OTP memory, in microseconds less one; 5 μs to 20 μs.

fields.name: OTPC_TIM2_US_T_VDS
fields.text: Time from turning on the OTP memory supply until the internal LDO can be turned on, in microseconds less one; 1 μs at least.

fields.name: OTPC_TIM2_US_T_PPS
fields.text: Time from turning on programming in the OTP memory until the first programming pulse, in microseconds less one; 5 μs to 20 μs.

fields.name: OTPC_TIM2_US_T_PPR
fields.text: Recovery time after a programming sequence, in microseconds less one; 5 μs to 100 μs.

fields.name: OTPC_TIM2_US_T_PWI
fields.text: Gap between successive programming pulses, in microseconds less one; 1 μs to 5 μs.

fields.name: OTPC_TIM2_US_T_PW
fields.text: Programming time of each bit, in microseconds less one; 10 μs to 20 μs.

fields.name: LED1_PWM_START_CYCLE
fields.text: Cycle at which the LED1 PWM goes high. When it exceeds the frequency setting, or equals the end cycle, the output stays 0.

fields.name: LED1_PWM_END_CYCLE
fields.text: Cycle at which the LED1 PWM goes low. When it exceeds the frequency setting while the start cycle does not, the output stays 1.

fields.name: LED2_PWM_START_CYCLE
fields.text: Cycle at which the LED2 PWM goes high. When it exceeds the frequency setting, or equals the end cycle, the output stays 0.

fields.name: LED2_PWM_END_CYCLE
fields.text: Cycle at which the LED2 PWM goes low. When it exceeds the frequency setting while the start cycle does not, the output stays 1.

fields.name: LED_PWM_FREQUENCY
fields.text: Frequency of PWM 1 and 2: period = PWM_CLK × (FREQ + 1).

fields.name: LED2_LOAD_SEL
fields.text: LED2 output current, 2.5 mA + LED2_LOAD_SEL × 2.5 mA, at most 20 mA.

fields.name: LED1_LOAD_SEL
fields.text: LED1 output current, 2.5 mA + LED1_LOAD_SEL × 2.5 mA, at most 20 mA.

fields.name: LED2_EN
fields.text: Enables LED2.

fields.name: LED1_EN
fields.text: Enables LED1.

fields.name: LED_TRIM
fields.text: Trims the LED current.

fields.name: SW_PAUSE_EN
fields.text: Software pause: 0 the PWMs run, 1 PWM 1 and PWM 2 are paused.

fields.name: PWM_ENABLE
fields.text: Enables PWM 1 and 2.

fields.name: QSPIC_DIS_CS
fields.text: In Manual mode, writing 1 deasserts the chip select (active low).

fields.name: QSPIC_EN_CS
fields.text: In Manual mode, writing 1 asserts the chip select (active low).

fields.name: QSPIC_SET_QUAD
fields.text: In Manual mode, writing 1 puts the bus in Quad mode.

fields.name: QSPIC_SET_DUAL
fields.text: In Manual mode, writing 1 puts the bus in Dual mode.

fields.name: QSPIC_SET_SINGLE
fields.text: In Manual mode, writing 1 puts the bus in single SPI mode.

fields.name: QSPIC_USE_32BA
fields.text: Address width of the external memory: 0 24-bit, 1 32-bit. In Auto mode the controller sends that many address bytes.

fields.name: QSPIC_BUF_LIM_EN
fields.text: Auto-mode reads only: what happens when the internal buffer fills mid-burst. 0 the flash access continues and QSPI_SCK is stopped until buffer space frees up; 1 the access ends, and a new one starts when addresses not in the buffer are requested. Either way the access ends when no read is pending.

fields.name: QSPIC_PCLK_MD
fields.text: Read pipe clock delay, 0 to 7, measured from the QSPI_SCK falling edge.

fields.name: QSPIC_RPIPE_EN
fields.text: Read data pipe: 0 off, with the sampling edge set by QSPIC_RXD_NEG; 1 on, with the sampling clock delay set by QSPI_PCLK_MD (the recommended setting).

fields.name: QSPIC_RXD_NEG
fields.text: Edge of QSPI_SCK that captures received data while the read pipe is off (QSPIC_RPIPE_EN = 0): 0 rising, 1 falling. The internal capture clock is skewed against the QSPI_SCK the memory sees; the read pipe with its programmable clock delay eases the read timing.

fields.name: QSPIC_HRDY_MD
fields.text: Manual mode only; for a QSPI clock much slower than the AMBA clock, so the bus is not held up. 0 accesses to QSPIC_WRITEDATA, QSPIC_READDATA and QSPIC_DUMMYDATA stall the bus through hready, and QSPIC_BUSY need not be polled; 1 they do not stall the bus, and QSPIC_BUSY in QSPIC_STATUS_REG must be polled to see completion. Auto mode always stalls through hready.

fields.name: QSPIC_IO3_DAT
fields.text: Level driven on the QSPI_IO3 pad while QSPI_IO3_OEN is 1.

fields.name: QSPIC_IO2_DAT
fields.text: Level driven on the QSPI_IO2 pad while QSPI_IO2_OEN is 1.

fields.name: QSPIC_IO3_OEN
fields.text: Direction of the QSPI_IO3 pad: 0 input, 1 output. Meant for driving /HOLD in SPI or Dual SPI mode only; with Auto mode (QSPIC_AUTO_MD = 1) and Quad SPI it must be 0.

fields.name: QSPIC_IO2_OEN
fields.text: Direction of the QSPI_IO2 pad: 0 input, 1 output. Meant for driving /WP in SPI or Dual SPI mode only; with Auto mode (QSPIC_AUTO_MD = 1) and Quad SPI it must be 0.

fields.name: QSPIC_CLK_MD
fields.text: QSPI_SCK clock mode: 0 Mode 0, QSPI_SCK low while QSPI_CS is high; 1 Mode 3, QSPI_SCK high while QSPI_CS is high.

fields.name: QSPIC_AUTO_MD
fields.text: Operating mode: 0 Manual, 1 Auto. It is read-only while an erase is under way (QSPIC_ERASE_EN).

fields.name: QSPIC_RECVDATA
fields.text: Data received in Manual mode after a read through QSPIC_READDATA_REG, valid with QSPIC_HRDY_MD=1 and QSPIC_BUSY=0.

fields.name: QSPIC_DMY_TX_MD
fields.text: SPI bus mode in the dummy-byte phase: 0x0 single, 0x1 dual, 0x2 quad, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_EXT_TX_MD
fields.text: SPI bus mode in the extra-byte phase: 0x0 single, 0x1 dual, 0x2 quad, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_ADR_TX_MD
fields.text: SPI bus mode in the address phase: 0x0 single, 0x1 dual, 0x2 quad, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_INST_TX_MD
fields.text: SPI bus mode in the instruction phase: 0x0 single, 0x1 dual, 0x2 quad, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_EXT_BYTE
fields.text: Extra byte sent after the address when QSPIC_EXT_BYTE_EN = 1, usually the mode bits of Dual/Quad SPI I/O instructions.

fields.name: QSPIC_INST_WB
fields.text: Instruction used for a wrapping burst when QSPIC_WRAP_MD is 1 and the burst's length and size match QSPIC_WRAP_LEN and QSPIC_WRAP_SIZE.

fields.name: QSPIC_INST
fields.text: Instruction used for incrementing bursts and single reads, and also when wrapping bursts are not supported (QSPIC_WRAP_MD).

fields.name: QSPIC_DMY_FORCE
fields.text: Dummy byte count: 0 set by QSPIC_DMY_NUM; 1 fixed at three, and QSPIC_DMY_NUM is ignored.

fields.name: QSPIC_CS_HIGH_MIN
fields.text: Fewest QSPI_SCK cycles the bus stays idle (QSPI_CS high) between two instructions to the flash; QSPIC_ERS_CS_HI covers some exceptions.

fields.name: QSPIC_WRAP_SIZE
fields.text: Access size for wrapping bursts under QSPIC_WRAP_MD: 0x0 8-bit byte, 0x1 16-bit half word, 0x2 32-bit word, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_WRAP_LEN
fields.text: Beat count for wrapping bursts under QSPIC_WRAP_MD: 0x0 4 beats, 0x1 8 beats, 0x2 16 beats, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_WRAP_MD
fields.text: Wrap mode: 0 QSPIC_INST is used for every access; 1 QSPIC_INST_WB is used for wrapping bursts of the length and size in QSPIC_WRAP_LEN and QSPIC_WRAP_SIZE, and QSPIC_INST for all else. Only for a flash that has a dedicated wrapping-burst instruction.

fields.name: QSPIC_INST_MD
fields.text: Instruction mode: 0 the instruction is sent on every burst; 1 only on the first access after Auto mode is selected.

fields.name: QSPIC_DMY_NUM
fields.text: Number of dummy bytes sent: 0x0 none, 0x1 one, 0x2 two, 0x3 four. Ignored when QSPIC_DMY_FORCE is set, which fixes the count at three.

fields.name: QSPIC_EXT_HF_DS
fields.text: With QSPIC_EXT_BYTE_EN = 1: 0 all of QSPIC_EXT_BYTE is sent; 1 the output is Hi-Z while bits [3:0] of QSPIC_EXT_BYTE are sent.

fields.name: QSPIC_EXT_BYTE_EN
fields.text: Extra byte enable: 0 QSPIC_EXT_BYTE is not sent, 1 it is sent.

fields.name: QSPIC_DAT_RX_MD
fields.text: SPI bus mode in the data phase: 0x0 single, 0x1 dual, 0x2 quad, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_BUSY
fields.text: SPI bus status: 0 idle; 1 active, with a read, write or dummy transfer under way. Meaningful only in Manual mode with QSPIC_HRDY_MD = 1.

fields.name: QSPIC_WRITEDATA
fields.text: Manual mode only: a write here sends the written data to the external memory in the bus mode selected (SPI, Dual, Quad). The access may be 32, 16 or 8 bits, and that many bits are sent.

fields.name: QSPIC_READDATA
fields.text: Manual mode only: a read here fetches data from the external memory in the bus mode selected (SPI, Dual, Quad). The access may be 32, 16 or 8 bits, and that many bits are fetched.

fields.name: QSPIC_DUMMYDATA
fields.text: Manual mode only: a write here sends clock pulses on the SPI bus, the QSPI_IOx pads hi-Z during the last one. The access may be 32, 16 or 8 bits; the pulse count is the access size over the bus width, 1, 2 or 4 for Single, Dual or Quad.

fields.name: QSPIC_ERS_STATE
fields.text: Read-only progress of a sector or block erase: 0x0 no erase, 0x1 erase request pending, 0x2 erase running, 0x3 erase suspended, 0x4 erase finishing, 0x5 to 0x7 reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_ERASE_EN
fields.text: Read-only in Manual mode (QSPIC_AUTO_MD = 0). In Auto mode, writing 1 asks for an erase of the block or sector at (QSPIC_ERS_ADDR, 12'b0); the bit clears itself when the erase ends and is read-only until then, and QSPIC_AUTO_MD is read-only too, keeping the controller in Auto mode.

fields.name: QSPIC_ERS_ADDR
fields.text: Address of the block or sector to erase. With 24-bit addressing (QSPIC_USE_32BA = 0) bits [23:12] give address bits [23:12] and bits [11:4] are ignored; with 32-bit addressing (QSPIC_USE_32BA = 1) bits [23:4] give address bits [31:12].

fields.name: QSPIC_RES_INST
fields.text: Code of the erase resume instruction.

fields.name: QSPIC_SUS_INST
fields.text: Code of the erase suspend instruction.

fields.name: QSPIC_WEN_INST
fields.text: Code of the write enable instruction.

fields.name: QSPIC_ERS_INST
fields.text: Code of the erase instruction.

fields.name: QSPIC_RESSUS_DLY
fields.text: Least delay between an erase resume (or the first erase command) and the next erase suspend: 0 the suspend starts at once; 1 to 63 the controller waits at least that many 222 kHz clock cycles, counted from the end of the resume or erase command.

fields.name: QSPIC_ERSRES_HLD
fields.text: AMBA hclk cycles, 0 to 15, the controller must go without flash read requests before it issues an erase or erase resume.

fields.name: QSPIC_ERS_CS_HI
fields.text: Fewest QSPI bus clock cycles QSPI_CS stays high after a write enable, erase, erase suspend or erase resume instruction.

fields.name: QSPIC_EAD_TX_MD
fields.text: QSPI bus mode while the erase command's address is sent: 0x0 single, 0x1 dual, 0x2 quad, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_RES_TX_MD
fields.text: QSPI bus mode while the resume instruction is sent: 0x0 single, 0x1 dual, 0x2 quad, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_SUS_TX_MD
fields.text: QSPI bus mode while the suspend instruction is sent: 0x0 single, 0x1 dual, 0x2 quad, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_WEN_TX_MD
fields.text: QSPI bus mode while the write enable instruction is sent: 0x0 single, 0x1 dual, 0x2 quad, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_ERS_TX_MD
fields.text: QSPI bus mode while the erase command's instruction byte is sent: 0x0 single, 0x1 dual, 0x2 quad, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_SEC_HF_DS
fields.text: Output during the second half, QSPIC_BRK_WRD[3:0]: 0 the controller drives the QSPI bus, 1 it leaves the bus Hi-Z. Useful only with QSPIC_BRK_EN = 1 and QSPIC_BRK_SZ = 1.

fields.name: QSPIC_BRK_TX_MD
fields.text: QSPI bus mode while the burst break sequence is sent: 0x0 single, 0x1 dual, 0x2 quad, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_BRK_SZ
fields.text: Burst break sequence length: 0 one byte, QSPIC_BRK_WRD[15:8]; 1 two bytes, QSPIC_BRK_WRD[15:0].

fields.name: QSPIC_BRK_EN
fields.text: Read burst break sequence, a command that makes the device leave continuous read mode: 0 not sent, 1 sent. It is sent when the controller is in Auto mode, QSPIC_INST_MD = 1, the last command to the device was a read, and the controller is about to send a command other than a read.

fields.name: QSPIC_BRK_WRD
fields.text: The read burst break sequence the controller sends to make the memory leave continuous read mode.

fields.name: QSPIC_STSDLY_SEL
fields.text: Timer for the wait before the flash status register is read after an erase or erase resume: 0 QSPIC_RESSTS_DLY, counting QSPI clock cycles; 1 QSPIC_RESSUS_DLY, counting 222 kHz clock cycles.

fields.name: QSPIC_RESSTS_DLY
fields.text: Least delay between an erase or erase resume instruction and the following status register read: 0 the read starts at once; 1 to 63 the controller waits at least that many QSPI_CLK cycles, counted from the end of the erase or resume command. QSPIC_STSDLY_SEL picks whether this timer is used.

fields.name: QSPIC_BUSY_VAL
fields.text: Level of the flash Busy bit that means busy: 0 busy when it reads 0, 1 busy when it reads 1.

fields.name: QSPIC_BUSY_POS
fields.text: Position of the Busy bit in the status byte, 7 to 0.

fields.name: QSPIC_RSTAT_RX_MD
fields.text: QSPI bus mode while the status is received in a status read: 0x0 single, 0x1 dual, 0x2 quad, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_RSTAT_TX_MD
fields.text: QSPI bus mode while the status read command's instruction byte is sent: 0x0 single, 0x1 dual, 0x2 quad, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_RSTAT_INST
fields.text: Code of the read status instruction, sent in its instruction phase.

fields.name: QSPIC_CHCKERASE
fields.text: Writing any value while an erase runs makes the controller read the flash status register and update QSPIC_ERASE_EN from the Busy bit.

fields.name: QSPIC_PADS_SLEW
fields.text: Slew rate of the QSPI pads, indicative values with 6 pF flash pin load, Vcc 1.8 V, 25°C and 16 mA drive: 0 (weak) 1.7 V/ns rising and 1.9 V/ns falling; 1 2.0 and 2.3 V/ns; 2 2.3 and 2.6 V/ns; 3 (strong) 2.4 and 2.7 V/ns.

fields.name: QSPIC_PADS_DRV
fields.text: Drive current of the QSPI pads: 0 4 mA, 1 8 mA, 2 12 mA, 3 16 mA.

fields.name: QSPIC_UCODE_X
fields.text: Word 0 of the controller's 16 × 32-bit microcode memory, which holds the external flash initialisation sequence; word X (1 to 15) sits at QSPIC_UCODE_START + 4×X.

fields.name: QSPIC_CTR_EN
fields.text: On-the-fly AES-CTR decryption of data read from flash, in Auto mode only: 0 off; 1 data between the start address in QSPIC_CTR_SADDR_REG and the end address in QSPIC_CTR_EADDR_REG is decrypted, data outside that range is not. The key is held in the QSPIC_CTR_KEY_x_y_REG set and the nonce in the QSPIC_CTR_NONCE_x_y_REG set. Manual mode has no decryption.

fields.name: QSPIC_CTR_SADDR
fields.text: Bits [31:10] of the flash start address of an encrypted image; bits [9:0] are taken as 0. Used only while decryption is on (QSPIC_CTR_CTRL_REG[QSPIC_CTR_EN]).

fields.name: QSPIC_CTR_EADDR
fields.text: Bits [31:10] of the flash end address of an encrypted image; bits [9:0] are taken as 0x3FF. Used only while decryption is on (QSPIC_CTR_CTRL_REG[QSPIC_CTR_EN]).

fields.name: QSPIC_CTR_NONCE_0_3
fields.text: Nonce bytes N0 to N3, held in bits [31:0] as N0 to N3 and making up counter-block bytes CTRB0 to CTRB3; N4 to N7 (CTRB4 to CTRB7) are in QSPIC_CTR_NONCE_4_7_REG. The 16-byte AES-CTR counter block CTRB0 to CTRB15 starts with the 8-byte nonce; hardware fills CTRB8 to CTRB15 from the address offset of the data within the encrypted image. Used only with QSPIC_CTR_CTRL_REG[QSPIC_CTR_EN] = 1; no encrypted address may be read while the nonce is being changed.

fields.name: QSPIC_CTR_NONCE_4_7
fields.text: Nonce bytes N4 to N7, the counter block's CTRB4 to CTRB7, working as QSPIC_CTR_NONCE_0_3 does.

fields.name: QSPIC_CTR_KEY_0_3
fields.text: Key bytes K0 to K3 of the 256-bit (32-byte, K0 to K31) AES-CTR key for on-the-fly decryption (QSPIC_CTR_CTRL_REG[QSPIC_CTR_EN] = 1). Each QSPIC_CTR_KEY_X_Y_REG[31:0] holds {KX..KY}: 0_3, 4_7, 8_11, 12_15, 16_19, 20_23, 24_27, 28_31. Used only while decryption is on; no encrypted address may be read while the key is being changed.

fields.name: QSPIC_CTR_KEY_4_7
fields.text: Key bytes K4 to K7, working as QSPIC_CTR_KEY_0_3 does.

fields.name: QSPIC_CTR_KEY_8_11
fields.text: Key bytes K8 to K11, working as QSPIC_CTR_KEY_0_3 does.

fields.name: QSPIC_CTR_KEY_12_15
fields.text: Key bytes K12 to K15, working as QSPIC_CTR_KEY_0_3 does.

fields.name: QSPIC_CTR_KEY_16_19
fields.text: Key bytes K16 to K19, working as QSPIC_CTR_KEY_0_3 does.

fields.name: QSPIC_CTR_KEY_20_23
fields.text: Key bytes K20 to K23, working as QSPIC_CTR_KEY_0_3 does.

fields.name: QSPIC_CTR_KEY_24_27
fields.text: Key bytes K24 to K27, working as QSPIC_CTR_KEY_0_3 does.

fields.name: QSPIC_CTR_KEY_28_31
fields.text: Key bytes K28 to K31, working as QSPIC_CTR_KEY_0_3 does.

fields.name: QSPIC_DIS_CS
fields.text: In Manual mode, writing 1 releases (deasserts) the active-low chip select.

fields.name: QSPIC_EN_CS
fields.text: In Manual mode, writing 1 asserts the active-low chip select.

fields.name: QSPIC_SET_QUAD
fields.text: In Manual mode, writing 1 switches the bus to Quad mode.

fields.name: QSPIC_SET_DUAL
fields.text: In Manual mode, writing 1 switches the bus to Dual mode.

fields.name: QSPIC_SET_SINGLE
fields.text: In Manual mode, writing 1 switches the bus to single-line SPI mode.

fields.name: QSPIC_CLK_FREE_EN
fields.text: Sets what QSPI_SCK does while QSPI_CS is high, used only when QSPIC_CS_MD=1. 0: one QSPI_SCK pulse follows each rising edge of QSPI_CS; 1: QSPI_SCK keeps running the whole time QSPI_CS is inactive.

fields.name: QSPIC_CS_MD
fields.text: Picks the QSPI_SCK edge that QSPI_CS changes on. 0: rising edge, and QSPI_SCK stays idle while QSPI_CS is high; 1: falling edge, with QSPI_SCK behaviour during QSPI_CS high set by QSPIC_CLK_FREE_EN.

fields.name: QSPIC_SRAM_EN
fields.text: Type of external memory on the controller. 0: serial Flash; 1: serial SRAM, which turns off erase suspend/resume (a write to QSPIC_ERASECTRL_REG[QSPIC_ERASE_EN] then does nothing) and makes the device's mapped space writable.

fields.name: QSPIC_USE_32BA
fields.text: Address width of the external memory, which sets how many address bytes the controller sends in Auto mode. 0: 24-bit addresses; 1: 32-bit addresses.

fields.name: QSPIC_FORCENSEQ_EN
fields.text: How an AMBA burst maps onto the QSPI bus. 0: as one QSPI burst, with the fewest command/address phases; 1: split into single accesses, each beat getting its own command/address/extra/data sequence with QSPI_CS low only for that access, which shortens CS-low time and lowers power at a performance cost when the QSPI clock is much faster than the AMBA clock.

fields.name: QSPIC_PCLK_MD
fields.text: Read-pipe sampling clock delay, measured from the QSPI_SCK falling edge.

fields.name: QSPIC_RPIPE_EN
fields.text: Read data pipe enable. 0: pipe off, sampling edge set by QSPIC_RXD_NEG; 1: pipe on, sampling clock delay set by QSPIC_PCLK_MD (the recommended setting).

fields.name: QSPIC_RXD_NEG
fields.text: Edge of QSPI_SCK that samples read data while the read pipe is off (QSPIC_RPIPE_EN=0). 0: rising edge; 1: falling edge. The internal sampling clock is skewed from the QSPI_SCK the memory sees, which is why a read pipe with programmable clock delay exists (QSPIC_RPIPE_EN).

fields.name: QSPIC_HRDY_MD
fields.text: Wait-state behaviour on accesses to QSPIC_WRITEDATA, QSPIC_READDATA and QSPIC_DUMMYDATA, Manual mode only; meant for a QSPI clock much slower than the AMBA clock, so the AMBA bus is not held. 0: hready wait states are added and QSPIC_BUSY need not be polled; 1: no wait states, and completion is found by polling QSPIC_STATUS_REG.QSPIC_BUSY. Auto mode always adds wait states.

fields.name: QSPIC_IO3_DAT
fields.text: Level driven on the QSPI_IO3 pad when QSPI_IO3_OEN is 1.

fields.name: QSPIC_IO2_DAT
fields.text: Level driven on the QSPI_IO2 pad when QSPI_IO2_OEN is 1.

fields.name: QSPIC_IO3_OEN
fields.text: Output enable for the QSPI_IO3 pad, for driving /HOLD in single or dual SPI only; keep 0 in Auto mode (QSPIC_AUTO_MD=1) with quad SPI. 0: pad is an input; 1: pad is an output.

fields.name: QSPIC_IO2_OEN
fields.text: Output enable for the QSPI_IO2 pad, for driving /WP in single or dual SPI only; keep 0 in Auto mode (QSPIC_AUTO_MD=1) with quad SPI. 0: pad is an input; 1: pad is an output.

fields.name: QSPIC_CLK_MD
fields.text: SPI clock mode of QSPI_SCK, working together with QSPIC_CS_MD and QSPIC_CLK_FREE_EN. 0: mode 0, QSPI_SCK low while QSPI_CS is high; 1: mode 3, QSPI_SCK high while QSPI_CS is high.

fields.name: QSPIC_AUTO_MD
fields.text: Operating mode. 0: Manual mode; 1: Auto mode. While an erase is in progress this bit becomes read-only (QSPIC_ERASE_EN).

fields.name: QSPIC_RECVDATA
fields.text: Holds data fetched from the external memory by a Manual-mode read of QSPIC_READDATA_REG, valid once QSPIC_HRDY_MD=1 and QSPIC_BUSY=0.

fields.name: QSPIC_DMY_TX_MD
fields.text: Bus width while dummy bytes are sent. 0x0: one data line (single SPI); 0x1: two lines (dual); 0x2: four lines (quad); 0x3: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_EXT_TX_MD
fields.text: Bus width while the extra byte is sent. 0x0: one data line (single SPI); 0x1: two lines (dual); 0x2: four lines (quad); 0x3: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_ADR_TX_MD
fields.text: Bus width while the address is sent. 0x0: one data line (single SPI); 0x1: two lines (dual); 0x2: four lines (quad); 0x3: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_INST_TX_MD
fields.text: Bus width while the instruction is sent. 0x0: one data line (single SPI); 0x1: two lines (dual); 0x2: four lines (quad); 0x3: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_EXT_BYTE
fields.text: Byte sent after the address when QSPIC_EXT_BYTE_EN=1, typically the mode bits of Dual/Quad I/O commands.

fields.name: QSPIC_INST_WB
fields.text: Instruction used for a wrapping burst when QSPIC_WRAP_MD=1 and the burst matches QSPIC_WRAP_LEN and QSPIC_WRAP_SIZE.

fields.name: QSPIC_INST
fields.text: Instruction used for incremental bursts and single reads, and for wrapping bursts when QSPIC_WRAP_MD does not select QSPIC_INST_WB.

fields.name: QSPIC_DMY_FORCE
fields.text: Forces three dummy bytes. 0: dummy-byte count comes from QSPIC_DMY_NUM; 1: three dummy bytes are sent and QSPIC_DMY_NUM is ignored.

fields.name: QSPIC_CS_HIGH_MIN
fields.text: Minimum number of QSPI_SCK cycles QSPI_CS stays high between two instructions; QSPIC_ERS_CS_HI and QSPIC_WR_CS_HIGH_MIN override it in their cases.

fields.name: QSPIC_WRAP_SIZE
fields.text: Data size of the wrapping burst used with QSPIC_WRAP_MD. 0x0: byte (8 bits); 0x1: half-word (16 bits); 0x2: word (32 bits); 0x3: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_WRAP_LEN
fields.text: Length of the wrapping burst used with QSPIC_WRAP_MD. 0x0: 4 beats; 0x1: 8 beats; 0x2: 16 beats; 0x3: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_WRAP_MD
fields.text: Wrap mode. 0: QSPIC_INST is sent on every access; 1: QSPIC_INST_WB is sent on wrapping bursts matching QSPIC_WRAP_LEN and QSPIC_WRAP_SIZE, and QSPIC_INST on all others. Only for a Flash that has a dedicated wrapping-burst instruction.

fields.name: QSPIC_INST_MD
fields.text: Instruction mode. 0: the instruction is sent on every burst access; 1: it is sent only on the first access after Auto mode is selected.

fields.name: QSPIC_DMY_NUM
fields.text: Number of dummy bytes sent. 0x0: none; 0x1: one; 0x2: two; 0x3: four. Ignored when QSPIC_DMY_FORCE is set, which sends three.

fields.name: QSPIC_EXT_HF_DS
fields.text: Extra half disable output, acting when QSPIC_EXT_BYTE_EN=1. 0: all of QSPIC_EXT_BYTE is driven; 1: the output goes hi-Z while bits [3:0] of QSPIC_EXT_BYTE are sent.

fields.name: QSPIC_EXT_BYTE_EN
fields.text: Extra byte enable. 0: QSPIC_EXT_BYTE is not sent; 1: QSPIC_EXT_BYTE is sent.

fields.name: QSPIC_DAT_RX_MD
fields.text: Bus width while data is received. 0x0: one data line (single SPI); 0x1: two lines (dual); 0x2: four lines (quad); 0x3: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_BUSY
fields.text: SPI bus state, valid only in Manual mode with QSPIC_HRDY_MD=1. 0: idle; 1: a read, write or dummy data transfer is in progress.

fields.name: QSPIC_WRITEDATA
fields.text: In Manual mode, a write here sends the written data to the memory in the selected bus mode; the access size (8, 16 or 32 bits) sets how many bits go out.

fields.name: QSPIC_READDATA
fields.text: In Manual mode, a read here fetches data from the memory in the selected bus mode; the access size (8, 16 or 32 bits) sets how many bits come in.

fields.name: QSPIC_DUMMYDATA
fields.text: In Manual mode, a write here clocks out dummy cycles: (AHB access size)/(bus width of 1, 2 or 4), with the QSPI_IOx pads hi-Z during the last clock; access size 8, 16 or 32 bits.

fields.name: QSPIC_ERS_STATE
fields.text: Read-only progress of a sector/block erase. 0x0: no erase; 0x1: erase request pending; 0x2: erase running; 0x3: erase suspended; 0x4: erase finishing; 0x5 to 0x7: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_ERASE_EN
fields.text: Erase request and status, for serial Flash only (read-only with QSPIC_SRAM_EN=1 or in Manual mode); in Auto mode writing 1 erases the sector at (QSPIC_ERS_ADDR, 12'b0), and the bit clears itself when done, staying read-only and holding QSPIC_AUTO_MD read-only until then.

fields.name: QSPIC_ERS_ADDR
fields.text: Address of the block/sector to erase: with 24-bit addressing bits [23:12] give address bits [23:12] and bits [11:4] are ignored; with 32-bit addressing bits [23:4] give address bits [31:12].

fields.name: QSPIC_RES_INST
fields.text: Opcode of the erase resume command.

fields.name: QSPIC_SUS_INST
fields.text: Opcode of the erase suspend command.

fields.name: QSPIC_WEN_INST
fields.text: Opcode of the write enable command.

fields.name: QSPIC_ERS_INST
fields.text: Opcode of the erase command.

fields.name: QSPIC_RESSUS_DLY
fields.text: Minimum delay from the last erase resume command (or the first erase command) to an erase suspend command, counted from the end of that command. 0x00: suspend at once; 0x01 to 0x3F: wait at least this many 288 kHz clock cycles before suspending.

fields.name: QSPIC_ERSRES_HLD
fields.text: Number of AMBA hclk cycles with no Flash read requests required before an erase or erase resume command is issued; 0x0 to 0xF.

fields.name: QSPIC_ERS_CS_HI
fields.text: Minimum QSPI_SCK cycles QSPI_CS is held high after each write-enable, erase, suspend or resume command.

fields.name: QSPIC_EAD_TX_MD
fields.text: Bus width while the erase command's address is sent. 0x0: one data line (single SPI); 0x1: two lines (dual); 0x2: four lines (quad); 0x3: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_RES_TX_MD
fields.text: Bus width while the erase resume command is sent. 0x0: one data line (single SPI); 0x1: two lines (dual); 0x2: four lines (quad); 0x3: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_SUS_TX_MD
fields.text: Bus width while the erase suspend command is sent. 0x0: one data line (single SPI); 0x1: two lines (dual); 0x2: four lines (quad); 0x3: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_WEN_TX_MD
fields.text: Bus width while the write-enable command is sent. 0x0: one data line (single SPI); 0x1: two lines (dual); 0x2: four lines (quad); 0x3: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_ERS_TX_MD
fields.text: Bus width while the erase command's opcode is sent. 0x0: one data line (single SPI); 0x1: two lines (dual); 0x2: four lines (quad); 0x3: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_SEC_HF_DS
fields.text: Output disable for the second half, QSPIC_BRK_WRD[3:0], of the read break sequence; matters only when QSPIC_BRK_SZ=1 and QSPIC_BRK_EN=1. 0: those bits are driven onto the bus; 1: the bus floats (hi-Z) for them.

fields.name: QSPIC_BRK_TX_MD
fields.text: Bus width while the read break sequence goes out. 0x0: one data line (single SPI); 0x1: two lines (dual); 0x2: four lines (quad); 0x3: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_BRK_SZ
fields.text: Length of the read break sequence. 0: one byte, QSPIC_BRK_WRD[15:8]; 1: two bytes, QSPIC_BRK_WRD[15:0].

fields.name: QSPIC_BRK_EN
fields.text: Enables the read break sequence, a command that takes the device out of continuous read mode. 0: not sent; 1: sent when the controller is in Auto mode, QSPIC_INST_MD=1, the last command to the device was a read, and the next command is not a read.

fields.name: QSPIC_BRK_WRD
fields.text: Read break sequence sent to make the memory leave continuous read mode.

fields.name: QSPIC_STSDLY_SEL
fields.text: Selects which timer sets the wait after an erase or erase resume command before the Flash status register is read. 0: QSPIC_RESSTS_DLY, counting QSPI clock cycles; 1: QSPIC_RESSUS_DLY, counting 288 kHz clock cycles.

fields.name: QSPIC_RESSTS_DLY
fields.text: Minimum delay from the end of an erase or erase resume command to reading the Flash status register, used when QSPIC_STSDLY_SEL selects it. 0x00: read at once; 0x01 to 0x3F: wait at least this many QSPI_CLK cycles first.

fields.name: QSPIC_BUSY_VAL
fields.text: Level of the Flash status Busy bit that means busy. 0: busy when the bit is 0; 1: busy when the bit is 1.

fields.name: QSPIC_BUSY_POS
fields.text: Position (0 to 7) of the Busy bit in the Flash status register.

fields.name: QSPIC_RSTAT_RX_MD
fields.text: Bus width while the status value is received after a read-status opcode. 0x0: one data line (single SPI); 0x1: two lines (dual); 0x2: four lines (quad); 0x3: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_RSTAT_TX_MD
fields.text: Bus width while the read-status opcode is sent. 0x0: one data line (single SPI); 0x1: two lines (dual); 0x2: four lines (quad); 0x3: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_RSTAT_INST
fields.text: Opcode of the read status command, sent in its instruction phase.

fields.name: QSPIC_CHCKERASE
fields.text: Writing any value during an erase makes the controller read the Flash status register and update QSPIC_ERASE_EN from the Busy bit; only in Auto mode with an erase in progress (QSPIC_ERASE_EN=1), and not for serial SRAM.

fields.name: QSPIC_PADS_SLEW
fields.text: Slew rate of the QSPI pads; typical figures at 6 pF Flash pin load, Vcc 1.8 V, 25 C and 16 mA drive. 0x0: rise 1.7 V/ns, fall 1.9 V/ns (weakest); 0x1: rise 2.0, fall 2.3 V/ns; 0x2: rise 2.3, fall 2.6 V/ns; 0x3: rise 2.4, fall 2.7 V/ns (strongest).

fields.name: QSPIC_PADS_DRV
fields.text: Drive current of the QSPI pads. 0x0: 4 mA; 0x1: 8 mA; 0x2: 12 mA; 0x3: 16 mA.

fields.name: QSPIC_WR_CS_HIGH_MIN
fields.text: Minimum QSPI_SCK cycles QSPI_CS stays high after a write command.

fields.name: QSPIC_WR_DAT_TX_MD
fields.text: Bus width while write data is sent. 0x0: one data line (single SPI); 0x1: two lines (dual); 0x2: four lines (quad); 0x3: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_WR_ADR_TX_MD
fields.text: Bus width while a write's address is sent. 0x0: one data line (single SPI); 0x1: two lines (dual); 0x2: four lines (quad); 0x3: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_WR_INST_TX_MD
fields.text: Bus width while a write's opcode is sent. 0x0: one data line (single SPI); 0x1: two lines (dual); 0x2: four lines (quad); 0x3: reserved.

fields.name: QSPIC_WR_INST
fields.text: Opcode used to write the external SRAM.

fields.name: QSPIC_T_CEM_CC
fields.text: Maximum time tCEM that QSPI_CS may stay low, in QSPI clock cycles (tCEM / QSPI clock period, capped at 0x3FF); used only when QSPIC_T_CEM_EN=1.

fields.name: QSPIC_T_CEM_EN
fields.text: Enables a limit tCEM on how long QSPI_CS stays active, acting only in Auto mode (QSPIC_AUTO_MD=1) with a serial SRAM (QSPIC_SRAM_EN=1); meant for a dynamic RAM that refreshes only while deselected. 0: no limit (also the behaviour whenever QSPIC_SRAM_EN=0 or QSPIC_AUTO_MD=0); 1: a burst read or write keeps QSPI_CS active at most QSPIC_T_CEM_CC QSPI clock periods, longer transfers being split into several bursts with CS-inactive gaps and extra commands, though at least one beat always completes. QSPIC_T_CEM_CC is to be rewritten whenever the QSPI clock frequency changes, and that frequency must stay high enough for a 32-bit read or write to fit within tCEM.

fields.name: QSPIC_MEMBLEN
fields.text: Burst behaviour of the external memory, used in Auto mode (QSPIC_AUTO_MD=1) to serve AHB burst requests the way the device needs. 0x0: incremental bursts of any length; 0x1: 4-byte wrapping bursts; 0x2: 8-byte; 0x3: 16-byte; 0x4: 32-byte; 0x5: 64-byte; 0x6 to 0x7: reserved. The device may first need its burst type set by a special instruction issued in Manual mode.

fields.name: RFMON_BREQ_FORCE
fields.text: Set to 1 when capture throughput nears the bus/memory capacity: the controller then claims the bus aggressively, reducing its availability to other masters.

fields.name: RFMON_CIRC_EN
fields.text: Set to 1 for circular mode: captured data is written continuously into the memory buffer whose start is RFMON_ADDR_REG and whose size is RFMON_LEN_REG, until software writes RFMON_PACK_EN to 0.

fields.name: RFMON_PACK_EN
fields.text: Writing 1 begins capture of test bus data. 0: not capturing; 1: capturing. Outside circular mode (RFMON_CIRC_EN=0) it clears itself after RFMON_LEN words; in circular mode (RFMON_CIRC_EN=1) it stays 1 until software clears it.

fields.name: RFMON_ADDR
fields.text: Bits [31:2] of the AHB address where captured data starts being stored; bits [1:0] are taken as 0.

fields.name: RFMON_LEN
fields.text: Number of words to capture, minus one.

fields.name: RFMON_OFLOW_STK
fields.text: Sticky FIFO overflow flag. 0: the transfer finished with no overflow; 1: at least one FIFO overflow happened. Cleared by writing 1.

fields.name: RFMON_ACTIVE
fields.text: Controller state. 0: idle; 1: capture and/or DMA transfer in progress. It goes to 1 when RFMON_PACK_EN is written 1 and back to 0 once capture has ended (RFMON_PACK_EN=0) and all data has reached memory.

fields.name: RFMON_CRV_ADDR
fields.text: Bits [31:2] of the AHB address of the next memory access; bits [1:0] are 0.

fields.name: RFMON_CRV_LEN
fields.text: Words still to transfer, minus one.

fields.name: RTC_CAL_DISABLE

fields.name: RTC_TIME_DISABLE

fields.name: RTC_HMS

fields.name: RTC_KEEP

fields.name: RTC_MOTOR_EVENT_PERIOD

fields.name: RTC_PDC_EVENT_PERIOD

fields.name: SMOTOR_MOI

fields.name: CYCLIC_MODE

fields.name: SNC_IRQ_ACK
fields.text: Writing 1 acknowledges the Sensor Node interrupt: it clears SNC_IRQ_EN and so drops the IRQ line to the CM33 and/or PDC; the CM33 sets it once it takes the interrupt. Writes are ignored unless SNC_IRQ_EN is set, and the bit clears itself along with SNC_IRQ_EN.

fields.name: SNC_IRQ_CONFIG
fields.text: Where the Sensor Node IRQ goes. 0x0: neither CM33 nor PDC, both lines held low whatever SNC_IRQ_EN is; 0x1: CM33, if SNC_IRQ_EN is set; 0x2: PDC, if SNC_IRQ_EN is set; 0x3: both, if SNC_IRQ_EN is set. The field is locked once SNC_IRQ_EN is set and cannot change until CM33 acknowledges the IRQ; after software sets SNC_IRQ_EN, only setting SNC_IRQ_ACK releases it.

fields.name: SNC_IRQ_EN
fields.text: When set, raises a level-sensitive IRQ to the CM33, the PDC or both as SNC_IRQ_CONFIG selects; once set, only SNC_IRQ_ACK clears it.

fields.name: SNC_BRANCH_LOOP_INIT
fields.text: Writing 1 zeroes the loop counter of the COBR branch command (iterative branch of up to 128 passes); clears itself on the next SNC clock.

fields.name: SNC_RESET
fields.text: Synchronous reset of the Sensor Node Controller: resets its state and returns SNC_PC_REG to the base address in SNC_BASE_REG (in the memory controller); clears itself on the next SNC clock. A command in progress may be cut short.

fields.name: BUS_ERROR_DETECT_EN
fields.text: Enables detection of system bus errors caused by Sensor Node register accesses to unmapped addresses; on an error BUS_ERROR_STATUS in SNC_STATUS_REG is set and execution carries on with the next command.

fields.name: SNC_SW_CTRL
fields.text: When set, the PDC enable of the Sensor Node is bypassed and SNC_EN starts and stops it; meant for debugging, and the Sensor Node base address must be programmed before setting it.

fields.name: SNC_EN
fields.text: Sensor Node enable, effective only when SNC_SW_CTRL is set (otherwise the PDC controls it); clearing it halts the Sensor Node after the current command finishes.

fields.name: SNC_PC_LOADED
fields.text: 0: the Sensor Node FSM drives the program counter, adding 4 after each 32-bit command word fetched; 1: the program counter has been loaded with a new value. Loading needs the Sensor Node stopped, so SNC_IS_STOPPED is checked first; the bit clears itself when the Sensor Node is restarted. Manual start and stop needs SNC_SW_CTRL and SNC_EN in SNC_CTRL_REG set, bypassing the PDC, for debugging.

fields.name: SNC_IS_STOPPED
fields.text: 0: Sensor Node running, FSM active; 1: Sensor Node stopped, FSM halted, left by setting SNC_CTRL_REG.SNC_EN while SNC_SW_CTRL is also set. This debug mode bypasses the PDC's enable. SNC_PC_REG accepts writes only while this bit is 1; otherwise writes to it are dropped.

fields.name: HARD_FAULT_STATUS
fields.text: 0: no opcode error; 1: an opcode error happened, the Sensor Node keeps executing and sets this bit for debugging. Once set it clears only when the Sensor Node restarts from its base address, through SNC_CTRL_REG.SNC_RESET or a stop and start, which is possible only with the PDC bypassed (SNC_EN and SNC_SW_CTRL in control).

fields.name: BUS_ERROR_STATUS
fields.text: 0: no system bus error; 1: a bus error happened, the Sensor Node keeps running and sets this flag for debugging. It returns to 0 only when the Sensor Node restarts from its base address.

fields.name: SNC_DONE_STATUS
fields.text: 0: the Sensor Node has not finished its program; 1: it has finished, and a pulse tells the PDC at the same time. Set only by executing the SLP (sleep) command, issued after all pending Sensor Node work; cleared when the Sensor Node restarts from its base address, either by clearing and setting SNC_CTRL_REG.SNC_EN again under software control or by SNC_RESET.

fields.name: GR_FLAG
fields.text: Sensor Node GR (greater) flag, written by the RDCGR command or by Sensor Node microcode. Held at 0 in the FSM initial state (PD_COM power-up or SNC_CTRL_REG.SNC_RESET); after a stop and reset it keeps its value, so clear it by software if the application needs 0. The CM33 and CM0+ should not write it, above all while the Sensor Node is running.

fields.name: EQ_FLAG
fields.text: Sensor Node EQ (equal/high) flag, written by the RDCBI command or by Sensor Node microcode. Held at 0 in the FSM initial state (PD_COM power-up or SNC_CTRL_REG.SNC_RESET); after a stop and reset it keeps its value, so clear it by software if the application needs 0. fields.name: RBR_THR_DLL
fields.text: Shared address for three registers. RBR (read): the byte received on sin (UART mode) or sir_in (infrared mode), valid only while LSR.DR is 1; with FIFOs off (FCR[0]=0) it must be read before the next byte lands or it is overwritten and an overrun error results; with FIFOs on (FCR[0]=1) it reads the head of the RX FIFO, and a byte arriving while the FIFO is full is lost (the FIFO contents are kept) with an overrun error. THR (write): the byte to send on sout (UART mode) or sir_out_n (infrared mode); write it only while LSR.THRE (LSR[5]) is 1; with FIFOs off, one write clears THRE and further writes before THRE sets again overwrite it; with FIFOs on and THRE set, up to the FIFO depth (16 by default) characters may be written, and writes to a full FIFO are lost. DLL (when LCR.DLAB, LCR[7], is 1): low 8 bits of the 16-bit baud divisor; DLH is at UART_IER_DLH_REG (offset 0x4). Baud rate = sclk / (16 x divisor); with DLL and DLH both 0 the baud clock stops and nothing is sent or received. After DLL or DLH is set, wait 8 or more cycles of the DW_apb_uart's slowest clock before any transfer.

fields.name: PTIME_DLH7
fields.text: IER.PTIME, programmable THRE interrupt mode enable: 1 turns on generation of the THRE interrupt, 0 turns it off. When LCR.DLAB is 1, bit 7 of DLH.

fields.name: DLH6_5
fields.text: When LCR.DLAB is 1, bits 6:5 of DLH.

fields.name: ELCOLR_DLH4
fields.text: IER.ELCOLR (read only), how the Overrun, Parity, Framing Error and Break Interrupt bits of LSR are cleared; reads always 0: they clear on a read of the RX FIFO (RBR) or of LSR. When LCR.DLAB is 1, bit 4 of DLH.

fields.name: EDSSI_DLH3
fields.text: IER: reserved. When LCR.DLAB is 1, bit 3 of DLH.

fields.name: ELSI_DLH2
fields.text: IER.ELSI, receiver line status interrupt enable (the highest-priority interrupt): 1 enables it, 0 disables it. When LCR.DLAB is 1, bit 2 of DLH.

fields.name: ETBEI_DLH1
fields.text: IER.ETBEI, transmit holding register empty interrupt enable (third-highest priority): 1 enables it, 0 disables it. When LCR.DLAB is 1, bit 1 of DLH.

fields.name: ERBFI_DLH0
fields.text: IER.ERBFI, received data available interrupt enable, which also covers the character timeout interrupt in FIFO mode with FIFOs on (second-highest priority): 1 enables them, 0 disables them. When LCR.DLAB is 1, bit 0 of DLH.

fields.name: IIR_FCR
fields.text: Read: IIR. Bits 7:6 FIFOSE show whether the FIFOs are on (00 off, 11 on); bits 5:4 reserved; bits 3:0 IID give the highest-priority pending interrupt: 0001 none, 0010 THR empty, 0100 RX data available, 0110 RX line status, 0111 busy detect, 1100 character timeout. Write: FCR. Bits 7:6 RT set the RX FIFO level that raises the received data available interrupt, deasserts rts_n under auto flow control, and in some modes asserts dma_rx_req_n: 00 one character, 01 quarter full, 10 half full, 11 two short of full. Bits 5:4 TET set the TX FIFO empty level that raises the THRE interrupt while that mode is on, and in some modes asserts dma_tx_req_n: 00 empty, 01 two characters, 10 quarter full, 11 half full. Bit 3 DMAM picks DMA signalling mode 0 or 1 for the dma_rx_req_n and dma_tx_req_n outputs. Bit 2 XFIFOR resets the TX FIFO control logic and treats the FIFO as empty; bit 1 RFIFOR does the same for the RX FIFO; both clear themselves. Bit 0 FIFOE turns the TX and RX FIFOs on (1) or off (0); any change of it resets the control logic of both FIFOs.

fields.name: UART_DLAB
fields.text: Divisor latch access: 1 gives read and write access to DLL and DLH for setting the baud rate; clear it after the baud rate is set to reach the other registers.

fields.name: UART_BC
fields.text: Break control: 1 sends a break, forcing the serial output to the spacing state (logic 0); outside loopback mode (MCR[4]) sout stays low until this bit is cleared.

fields.name: UART_EPS
fields.text: Even parity select, writable only while USR[0] is 0 (UART not busy); applies when LCR.PEN is 1. 1: an even number of logic 1s is sent and checked. 0: an odd number.

fields.name: UART_PEN
fields.text: Parity enable, writable only while USR[0] is 0 (UART not busy): 1 generates parity on sent characters and checks it on received ones, 0 turns parity off.

fields.name: UART_STOP
fields.text: Number of stop bits sent and received per character: 0 gives one stop bit; 1 gives one and a half when LCR[1:0] (DLS) is 0 (5 data bits), else two. Whatever the setting, only the first stop bit is checked on receive.

fields.name: UART_DLS
fields.text: Data length select, the data bits per character sent and received: 00 five, 01 six, 10 seven, 11 eight.

fields.name: UART_LB
fields.text: Loopback, a diagnostic test mode; all interrupts keep working. In UART mode (MCR[6]=0, SIR_MODE off) sout is held high and the serial output is looped back to sin internally; dsr_n, cts_n, ri_n and dcd_n are cut off, and dtr_n, rts_n, out1_n and out2_n feed those inputs internally. In infrared mode (MCR[6]=1) sir_out_n is held low and the serial output is inverted and looped back to sir_in.

fields.name: UART_RFE
fields.text: Receiver FIFO error, meaningful only with FIFOs on (FCR[0]=1): 1 when the RX FIFO holds one or more characters with a parity error, a framing error or a break, 0 when none. Cleared by an LSR read once the erroneous character is at the head of the RX FIFO and no later errors are in it.

fields.name: UART_TEMT
fields.text: Transmitter empty: with FIFOs on (FCR[0]=1), set once the TX FIFO and the shift register hold nothing; with FIFOs off, set once THR and the shift register hold nothing.

fields.name: UART_THRE
fields.text: Transmit holding register empty. With THRE mode off (IER[7]=0), with or without FIFOs, set when THR or the TX FIFO is empty: it sets when data moves from THR or the TX FIFO into the transmitter shift register and nothing new has been written, and raises the THRE interrupt if that is enabled. With both THRE mode and FIFOs on (IER[7]=1, FCR[0]=1) it instead shows the TX FIFO is full and no longer drives the THRE interrupt, which then follows the FCR[5:4] threshold.

fields.name: UART_BI
fields.text: Break interrupt: set when a break is detected, sin held at logic 0 longer than start + data + parity + stop bit times. In FIFO mode the break character passes through the FIFO and the bit shows when that character reaches the top. In non-FIFO mode it shows at once and stays until LSR is read. A read of LSR clears it.

fields.name: UART_FE
fields.text: Framing error: 1 when the receiver finds no valid stop bit, 0 otherwise. In FIFO mode it shows when the offending character reaches the head of the FIFO. After a framing error the UART resynchronises by taking the error to be the next character's start bit and then receiving its data, parity and stop bits. It is also set when a break interrupt occurs (LSR[4], BI). An LSR read clears it.

fields.name: UART_PE
fields.text: Parity error: 1 when a received character fails parity while LCR[3] (PEN) is 1, 0 otherwise. In FIFO mode it shows when the offending character reaches the head of the FIFO. It is also set when a break interrupt occurs (LSR[4], BI). An LSR read clears it.

fields.name: UART_OE
fields.text: Overrun error: 1 when a character arrives before the previous one was read, 0 otherwise. Without FIFOs the new character overwrites the one in RBR; in FIFO mode it arrives while the FIFO is full, the FIFO keeps its contents and the character in the receive shift register is lost. An LSR read clears it.

fields.name: UART_DR
fields.text: Data ready: 1 while RBR or the RX FIFO holds at least one character, 0 when none. Cleared by reading RBR without FIFOs, or when the RX FIFO empties in FIFO mode.

fields.name: UART_SCRATCH_PAD
fields.text: Scratch byte for software; the UART does nothing with it.

fields.name: SRBR_STHRx
fields.text: Shadow of RBR (read) and THR (write), one of sixteen 32-bit addresses for burst access by the master. Read: the byte received on sin (UART mode) or sir_in (infrared mode), valid only while LSR.DR is 1; with FIFOs off (FCR[0]=0) it must be read before the next byte arrives or it is overwritten and an overrun error results; with FIFOs on (FCR[0]=1) it reads the head of the RX FIFO, and a byte arriving while that FIFO is full is lost, the FIFO contents kept, with an overrun error. Write: the byte to send on sout (UART mode) or sir_out_n (infrared mode), to be written only while LSR[5] (THRE) is 1; with FIFOs off one write clears THRE and further writes before THRE sets again overwrite it; with FIFOs on and THRE set, characters up to the configured FIFO depth (16 by default) may be written, and a write to a full FIFO is lost.
