fields.name: UART_RFF
fields.text: Receive FIFO full: 1 when the RX FIFO is completely full, 0 otherwise; clears once the RX FIFO is no longer full.

fields.name: UART_RFNE
fields.text: Receive FIFO not empty: 1 when the RX FIFO holds one or more entries, 0 when it is empty; clears when the RX FIFO empties.

fields.name: UART_TFE
fields.text: Transmit FIFO empty: 1 when the TX FIFO is completely empty, 0 otherwise; clears once the TX FIFO is no longer empty.

fields.name: UART_TFNF
fields.text: Transmit FIFO not full: 1 when the TX FIFO has room, 0 when it is full; clears when the TX FIFO fills.

fields.name: UART_BUSY
fields.text: UART busy: 1 while a serial transfer is in progress, 0 when the UART is idle or inactive. It can read 0 while another device's character is starting: with THR and RBR empty and nothing being sent, a start bit just arriving is not seen as valid until mid-bit, a delay set by the baud divisor. With a second system clock (CLOCK_MODE enabled) the setting of this bit also lags by several cycles of the slower clock.

fields.name: UART_TRANSMIT_FIFO_LEVEL
fields.text: Number of entries in the TX FIFO.

fields.name: UART_RECEIVE_FIFO_LEVEL
fields.text: Number of entries in the RX FIFO.

fields.name: UART_XFR
fields.text: TX FIFO reset, a shadow of FCR[2] so the transmit FIFO can be reset without keeping the last FCR value: resets the FIFO's control logic and treats it as empty. Clears itself.

fields.name: UART_RFR
fields.text: RX FIFO reset, a shadow of FCR[1] so the receive FIFO can be reset without keeping the last FCR value: resets the FIFO's control logic and treats it as empty. Clears itself.

fields.name: UART_UR
fields.text: UART reset: resets the UART asynchronously and releases the reset synchronously; with two clocks, both the pclk and sclk domains are reset.

fields.name: UART_SHADOW_BREAK_CONTROL
fields.text: Shadow of the break bit LCR[6], writable without a read-modify-write of LCR: 1 sends a break, forcing the serial output to the spacing state (logic 0); outside loopback mode (MCR[4]) sout stays low until the bit is cleared.

fields.name: UART_SHADOW_DMA_MODE
fields.text: Shadow DMA mode, a separate copy of FCR[3] (DMAM) that can be written alone, without keeping and masking the last FCR value. Picks DMA signalling mode for the dma_rx_req_n and dma_tx_req_n outputs: 0 mode 0, 1 mode 1.

fields.name: UART_SHADOW_FIFO_ENABLE
fields.text: Shadow of the FIFO enable bit FCR[0], writable without keeping and masking the last FCR value: turns the TX and RX FIFOs on or off. Clearing it after they were on resets the controller part of both FIFOs.

fields.name: UART_SHADOW_RCVR_TRIGGER
fields.text: Shadow RCVR trigger, a separate copy of FCR[7:6] that can be written alone, without keeping and masking the last FCR value. Sets the RX FIFO level that raises the received data available interrupt, and that asserts dma_rx_req_n when FCR[3] (DMA mode) is 1: 00 one character, 01 quarter full, 10 half full, 11 two short of full.

fields.name: UART_SHADOW_TX_EMPTY_TRIGGER
fields.text: Shadow TX empty trigger, a separate copy of FCR[5:4] that can be written alone, without keeping and masking the last FCR value. Sets the TX FIFO empty level that raises the THRE interrupt while that mode is on: 00 empty, 01 two characters, 10 quarter full, 11 half full.

fields.name: UART_HALT_TX
fields.text: Halt TX: 1 stops transmission so the master can fill the TX FIFO, 0 lets it run. Applies when FIFOs are implemented and on; with FIFOs off it has no effect.

fields.name: UART_DMASA
fields.text: DMA software acknowledge, for ending a transfer on an error, such as the DMA disabling the channel: the UART de-asserts its request and single signals for both TX and RX. Clears itself.

fields.name: UART_DLF
fields.text: Fractional part of the baud divisor, added to the integer divisor in DLH and DLL; worth UART_DLF/16.

fields.name: UART_UCV
fields.text: Component version.

fields.name: UART_CTR
fields.text: Component type.

fields.name: RBR_THR_9BIT
fields.text: With 9-bit data on: read gives receive buffer bit 8; write sets transmit buffer bit 8 when LCR_EXT[3] is 1.

fields.name: RBR_THR_DLL
fields.text: Shared address for three registers. RBR (read): the byte received on sin (UART mode) or sir_in (infrared mode), valid only while LSR.DR is 1; with FIFOs off (FCR[0]=0) it must be read before the next byte lands or it is overwritten and an overrun error results; with FIFOs on (FCR[0]=1) it reads the head of the RX FIFO, and a byte arriving while the FIFO is full is lost (the FIFO contents are kept) with an overrun error. THR (write): the byte to send on sout (UART mode) or sir_out_n (infrared mode); write it only while LSR.THRE (LSR[5]) is 1; with FIFOs off, one write clears THRE and further writes before THRE sets again overwrite it; with FIFOs on and THRE set, up to the FIFO depth (16 by default) characters may be written, and writes to a full FIFO are lost. DLL (when LCR.DLAB, LCR[7], is 1): low 8 bits of the 16-bit baud divisor; DLH is at UART_IER_DLH_REG (offset 0x4). Baud rate = sclk / (16 x divisor); with DLL and DLH both 0 the baud clock stops and nothing is sent or received. After DLL or DLH is set, wait 8 or more cycles of the DW_apb_uart's slowest clock before any transfer.

fields.name: PTIME_DLH7
fields.text: IER.PTIME, programmable THRE interrupt mode enable: 1 turns on generation of the THRE interrupt, 0 turns it off. When LCR.DLAB is 1, bit 7 of DLH.

fields.name: DLH6_5
fields.text: When LCR.DLAB is 1, bits 6:5 of DLH.

fields.name: ELCOLR_DLH4
fields.text: IER.ELCOLR (read only), how LSR's overrun, parity and framing error bits and its break interrupt bit are cleared: 0, they clear on a read of the RX FIFO (RBR) or of LSR. When LCR.DLAB is 1, bit 4 of DLH.

fields.name: EDSSI_DLH3
fields.text: IER.EDSSI, modem status interrupt enable (fourth-highest priority): 1 enables it, 0 disables it. When LCR.DLAB is 1, bit 3 of DLH.

fields.name: ELSI_DLH2
fields.text: IER.ELSI, receiver line status interrupt enable (the highest-priority interrupt): 1 enables it, 0 disables it. When LCR.DLAB is 1, bit 2 of DLH.

fields.name: ETBEI_DLH1
fields.text: IER.ETBEI, transmit holding register empty interrupt enable (third-highest priority): 1 enables it, 0 disables it. When LCR.DLAB is 1, bit 1 of DLH.

fields.name: ERBFI_DLH0
fields.text: IER.ERBFI, received data available interrupt enable, which also covers the character timeout interrupt in FIFO mode with FIFOs on (second-highest priority): 1 enables them, 0 disables them. When LCR.DLAB is 1, bit 0 of DLH.

fields.name: IIR_FCR
fields.text: Read: IIR. Bits 7:6 FIFOSE show whether the FIFOs are on (00 off, 11 on); bits 5:4 reserved; bits 3:0 IID give the highest-priority pending interrupt: 0001 none, 0010 THR empty, 0100 RX data available, 0110 RX line status, 0111 busy detect, 1100 character timeout. Write: FCR. Bits 7:6 RT set the RX FIFO level that raises the received data available interrupt, deasserts rts_n under auto flow control, and in some modes asserts dma_rx_req_n: 00 one character, 01 quarter full, 10 half full, 11 two short of full. Bits 5:4 TET set the TX FIFO empty level that raises the THRE interrupt while that mode is on, and in some modes asserts dma_tx_req_n: 00 empty, 01 two characters, 10 quarter full, 11 half full. Bit 3 DMAM picks DMA signalling mode 0 or 1 for the dma_rx_req_n and dma_tx_req_n outputs. Bit 2 XFIFOR resets the TX FIFO control logic and treats the FIFO as empty; bit 1 RFIFOR does the same for the RX FIFO; both clear themselves. Bit 0 FIFOE turns the TX and RX FIFOs on (1) or off (0); any change of it resets the control logic of both FIFOs.

fields.name: UART_DLAB
fields.text: Divisor latch access: 1 gives read and write access to DLL and DLH for setting the baud rate; clear it after the baud rate is set to reach the other registers.

fields.name: UART_BC
fields.text: Break control: 1 sends a break, forcing the serial output to the spacing state (logic 0); outside loopback mode (MCR[4]) sout stays low until this bit is cleared.

fields.name: UART_SP
fields.text: Stick parity, writable only while USR[0] is 0 (UART not busy): forces the parity bit. With PEN, EPS and this bit all 1, parity is sent and checked as logic 0; with PEN and this bit 1 and EPS 0, as logic 1. 0 turns stick parity off.

fields.name: UART_EPS
fields.text: Even parity select, writable only while USR[0] is 0 (UART not busy); applies when LCR.PEN is 1. 1: an even number of logic 1s is sent and checked. 0: an odd number.

fields.name: UART_PEN
fields.text: Parity enable, writable only while USR[0] is 0 (UART not busy): 1 generates parity on sent characters and checks it on received ones, 0 turns parity off.

fields.name: UART_STOP
fields.text: Number of stop bits sent and received per character: 0 gives one stop bit; 1 gives one and a half when LCR[1:0] (DLS) is 0 (5 data bits), else two. Whatever the setting, only the first stop bit is checked on receive.

fields.name: UART_DLS
fields.text: Data length select, the data bits per character sent and received: 00 five, 01 six, 10 seven, 11 eight.

fields.name: UART_AFCE
fields.text: Auto flow control enable: with FIFOs on, 1 turns on the auto flow control features, 0 turns them off.

fields.name: UART_LB
fields.text: Loopback, a diagnostic test mode; all interrupts keep working. sout is held high and the serial output is looped back to sin internally; dsr_n, cts_n, ri_n and dcd_n are cut off, and dtr_n and rts_n feed the modem inputs internally.

fields.name: UART_RTS
fields.text: Request to send: drives the rts_n output, which tells the modem or data set the UART is ready to exchange data. Without auto flow control (MCR[5]=0), writing 1 drives rts_n low and writing 0 de-asserts it. With auto flow control (MCR[5]=1) and FIFOs on (FCR[0]=1), rts_n follows this bit gated by the RX FIFO threshold (inactive high above it). In loopback mode (MCR[4]=1) rts_n is held inactive high and this bit loops back internally to an input.

fields.name: UART_ADDR_RCVD
fields.text: Address received, used with 9-bit data mode (LCR_EXT[0]=1): 1 when the received character's 9th bit is 1, marking it an address; 0 marks it data. In FIFO mode it shows when that character reaches the head of the FIFO. An LSR read clears it; it must be cleared before the next address byte arrives, or software cannot tell successive address interrupts apart.

fields.name: UART_RFE
fields.text: Receiver FIFO error, meaningful only with FIFOs on (FCR[0]=1): 1 when the RX FIFO holds one or more characters with a parity error, a framing error or a break, 0 when none. Cleared by an LSR read once the erroneous character is at the head of the RX FIFO and no later errors are in it.

fields.name: UART_TEMT
fields.text: Transmitter empty: with FIFOs on (FCR[0]=1), set once the TX FIFO and the shift register hold nothing; with FIFOs off, set once THR and the shift register hold nothing.

fields.name: UART_THRE
fields.text: Transmit holding register empty. With THRE mode off (IER[7]=0), with or without FIFOs, set when THR or the TX FIFO is empty: it sets when data moves from THR or the TX FIFO into the transmitter shift register and nothing new has been written, and raises the THRE interrupt if that is enabled. With both THRE mode and FIFOs on (IER[7]=1, FCR[0]=1) it instead shows the TX FIFO is full and no longer drives the THRE interrupt, which then follows the FCR[5:4] threshold.

fields.name: UART_BI
fields.text: Break interrupt: in UART mode (SIR_MODE disabled), set when sin is held at logic 0 longer than start + data + parity + stop bit times. In FIFO mode the break character passes through the FIFO and the bit shows when that character reaches the top. In non-FIFO mode it shows at once and stays until LSR is read. A read of LSR clears it.

fields.name: UART_FE
fields.text: Framing error: 1 when the receiver finds no valid stop bit, 0 otherwise. In FIFO mode it shows when the offending character reaches the head of the FIFO. After a framing error the UART resynchronises by taking the error to be the next character's start bit and then receiving its data, parity and stop bits. It is also set when a break interrupt occurs (LSR[4], BI). An LSR read clears it.

fields.name: UART_PE
fields.text: Parity error: 1 when a received character fails parity while LCR[3] (PEN) is 1, 0 otherwise. In FIFO mode it shows when the offending character reaches the head of the FIFO. It is also set when a break interrupt occurs (LSR[4], BI). An LSR read clears it.

fields.name: UART_OE
fields.text: Overrun error: 1 when a character arrives before the previous one was read, 0 otherwise. Without FIFOs the new character overwrites the one in RBR; in FIFO mode it arrives while the FIFO is full, the FIFO keeps its contents and the character in the receive shift register is lost. An LSR read clears it.

fields.name: UART_DR
fields.text: Data ready: 1 while RBR or the RX FIFO holds at least one character, 0 when none. Cleared by reading RBR without FIFOs, or when the RX FIFO empties in FIFO mode.

fields.name: UART_CTS
fields.text: Clear to send, the inverse of the cts_n input: 1 when cts_n is asserted (logic 0), meaning the modem or data set can exchange data with the UART; 0 when it is deasserted (logic 1). In loopback mode (MCR[4]=1) it equals MCR[1] (RTS).

fields.name: UART_DCTS
fields.text: Delta clear to send: 1 when cts_n has changed since MSR was last read, 0 when not. An MSR read clears it. In loopback mode (MCR[4]=1) it follows changes of MCR[1] (RTS). If it is 0 and cts_n is asserted (low) through a reset of any kind, it is set when the reset ends while cts_n stays asserted.

fields.name: UART_SCRATCH_PAD
fields.text: Scratch byte for software; the UART does nothing with it.

fields.name: SRBR_STHRx
fields.text: Shadow of RBR (read) and THR (write), one of sixteen 32-bit addresses for burst access by the master. Read: the byte received on sin (UART mode) or sir_in (infrared mode), valid only while LSR.DR is 1; with FIFOs off (FCR[0]=0) it must be read before the next byte arrives or it is overwritten and an overrun error results; with FIFOs on (FCR[0]=1) it reads the head of the RX FIFO, and a byte arriving while that FIFO is full is lost, the FIFO contents kept, with an overrun error. Write: the byte to send on sout (UART mode) or sir_out_n (infrared mode), to be written only while LSR[5] (THRE) is 1; with FIFOs off one write clears THRE and further writes before THRE sets again overwrite it; with FIFOs on and THRE set, characters up to the configured FIFO depth (16 by default) may be written, and a write to a full FIFO is lost.

fields.name: UART_RFF
fields.text: Receive FIFO full: 1 when the RX FIFO is completely full, 0 otherwise; clears once the RX FIFO is no longer full.

fields.name: UART_RFNE
fields.text: Receive FIFO not empty: 1 when the RX FIFO holds one or more entries, 0 when it is empty; clears when the RX FIFO empties.

fields.name: UART_TFE
fields.text: Transmit FIFO empty: 1 when the TX FIFO is completely empty, 0 otherwise; clears once the TX FIFO is no longer empty.

fields.name: UART_TFNF
fields.text: Transmit FIFO not full: 1 when the TX FIFO has room, 0 when it is full; clears when the TX FIFO fills.

fields.name: UART_BUSY
fields.text: UART busy: 1 while a serial transfer is in progress, 0 when the UART is idle. It can read 0 while a new character's start bit has just arrived from another device, with THR and RBR empty and no transmission running, since a start bit is recognized only at mid-bit, a delay set by the baud divisor; with a second system clock (CLOCK_MODE enabled) setting the bit also lags by several cycles of the slower clock.

fields.name: UART_TRANSMIT_FIFO_LEVEL
fields.text: Number of entries in the TX FIFO.

fields.name: UART_RECEIVE_FIFO_LEVEL
fields.text: Number of entries in the RX FIFO.

fields.name: UART_XFR
fields.text: TX FIFO reset, a shadow of FCR[2] so the transmit FIFO can be reset without keeping the last FCR value: resets the FIFO's control logic and treats it as empty. Clears itself.

fields.name: UART_RFR
fields.text: RX FIFO reset, a shadow of FCR[1] so the receive FIFO can be reset without keeping the last FCR value: resets the FIFO's control logic and treats it as empty. Clears itself.

fields.name: UART_UR
fields.text: UART reset: resets the UART asynchronously and releases the reset synchronously; with two clocks, both the pclk and sclk domains are reset.

fields.name: UART_SHADOW_REQUEST_TO_SEND
fields.text: Shadow of the RTS bit MCR[1], writable without a read-modify-write of MCR: drives rts_n, which tells the modem or data set the UART is ready to exchange data. Without auto flow control (MCR[5]=0), writing 1 drives rts_n low. With auto flow control (MCR[5]=1) and FIFOs on (FCR[0]=1), rts_n follows the bit gated by the RX FIFO threshold (inactive high above it). In loopback mode (MCR[4]=1) rts_n is held inactive high and the bit loops back internally to an input.

fields.name: UART_SHADOW_BREAK_CONTROL
fields.text: Shadow of the break bit LCR[6], writable without a read-modify-write of LCR: 1 sends a break, forcing the serial output to the spacing state (logic 0); outside loopback mode (MCR[4]) sout stays low until the bit is cleared.

fields.name: UART_SHADOW_DMA_MODE
fields.text: Shadow DMA mode, a separate copy of FCR[3] (DMAM) that can be written alone, without keeping and masking the last FCR value. Picks DMA signalling mode for the dma_rx_req_n and dma_tx_req_n outputs: 0 mode 0, 1 mode 1.

fields.name: UART_SHADOW_FIFO_ENABLE
fields.text: Shadow of the FIFO enable bit FCR[0], writable without keeping and masking the last FCR value: turns the TX and RX FIFOs on or off. Clearing it after they were on resets the controller part of both FIFOs.

fields.name: UART_SHADOW_RCVR_TRIGGER
fields.text: Shadow RCVR trigger, a separate copy of FCR[7:6] that can be written alone, without keeping and masking the last FCR value. Sets the RX FIFO level that raises the received data available interrupt, and that asserts dma_rx_req_n when FCR[3] (DMA mode) is 1: 00 one character, 01 quarter full, 10 half full, 11 two short of full.

fields.name: UART_SHADOW_TX_EMPTY_TRIGGER
fields.text: Shadow TX empty trigger, a separate copy of FCR[5:4] that can be written alone, without keeping and masking the last FCR value. Sets the TX FIFO empty level that raises the THRE interrupt while that mode is on: 00 empty, 01 two characters, 10 quarter full, 11 half full.

fields.name: UART_HALT_TX
fields.text: Halt TX: 1 stops transmission so the master can fill the TX FIFO, 0 lets it run. Applies when FIFOs are implemented and on; with FIFOs off it has no effect.

fields.name: UART_DMASA
fields.text: DMA software acknowledge, for ending a transfer on an error, such as the DMA disabling the channel: the UART de-asserts its request and single signals for both TX and RX. Clears itself.

fields.name: UART_DLF
fields.text: Fractional part of the baud divisor, added to the integer divisor in DLH and DLL; worth UART_DLF/16.

fields.name: UART_RAR
fields.text: Receive address to match: when a character arrives with its 9th bit set, its lower 8 bits are compared with this value; on a match, following characters with the 9th bit 0 are taken as data until the next address byte. Used only with LCR_EXT.ADDR_MATCH (LCR_EXT[1]) and LCR_EXT.DLS_E (LCR_EXT[0]) both 1; write it only while the UART is not busy.

fields.name: UART_TAR
fields.text: Transmit address: with LCR_EXT.DLS_E (LCR_EXT[0]) on and LCR_EXT.SEND_ADDR (LCR_EXT[2]) set, the UART sends a 9-bit character with the 9th bit 1 and these 8 bits as the address. Only the address goes here; data is written to THR. SEND_ADDR is cleared by hardware once the address starts going out.

fields.name: UART_TRANSMIT_MODE
fields.text: Transmit mode for 9-bit transfers. 1: THR and STHR are 9 bits wide and each write carries its own 9th bit, 1 for an address and 0 for data; the transmit address register (TAR) is not used. 0: THR and STHR are 8 bits wide; the address goes in TAR, data in THR/STHR, and SEND_ADDR says when the address is sent.

fields.name: UART_SEND_ADDR
fields.text: Send address, the trigger for sending the address while transmitting. 1: a 9-bit character goes out with the 9th bit 1 and the other 8 bits from the transmit address register. 0: 9-bit characters go out with the 9th bit 0 and the other 8 bits from the TX FIFO, written through the 8-bit THR/STHR. Hardware clears it after the address character is sent; it is not to be written 0. Applies only when DLS_E is 1 and TRANSMIT_MODE is 0.

fields.name: UART_ADDR_MATCH
fields.text: Address match mode for receive, applies only when DLS_E is 1. 1: the UART waits for a character with its 9th bit 1 and compares it with the receive address match register; on a match the characters that follow are taken as data and received. 0: normal mode; every 9-bit character is received into the RX FIFO, and software reads it and tells address from data.

fields.name: UART_DLS_E
fields.text: DLS extension: turns on 9-bit data for transmit and receive.

fields.name: UART_UCV
fields.text: Component version.

fields.name: UART_CTR
fields.text: Component type.

fields.name: RBR_THR_9BIT
fields.text: With 9-bit data on: read gives receive buffer bit 8; write sets transmit buffer bit 8 when LCR_EXT[3] is 1.

fields.name: RBR_THR_DLL
fields.text: Shared address for three registers. RBR (read): the byte received on sin (UART mode) or sir_in (infrared mode), valid only while LSR.DR is 1; with FIFOs off (FCR[0]=0) it must be read before the next byte lands or it is overwritten and an overrun error results; with FIFOs on (FCR[0]=1) it reads the head of the RX FIFO, and a byte arriving while the FIFO is full is lost (the FIFO contents are kept) with an overrun error. THR (write): the byte to send on sout (UART mode) or sir_out_n (infrared mode); write it only while LSR.THRE (LSR[5]) is 1; with FIFOs off, one write clears THRE and further writes before THRE sets again overwrite it; with FIFOs on and THRE set, up to the FIFO depth (16 by default) characters may be written, and writes to a full FIFO are lost. DLL (when LCR.DLAB, LCR[7], is 1): low 8 bits of the 16-bit baud divisor; DLH is at UART_IER_DLH_REG (offset 0x4). Baud rate = sclk / (16 x divisor); with DLL and DLH both 0 the baud clock stops and nothing is sent or received. After DLL or DLH is set, wait 8 or more cycles of the DW_apb_uart's slowest clock before any transfer.

fields.name: PTIME_DLH7
fields.text: IER.PTIME, programmable THRE interrupt mode enable: 1 turns on generation of the THRE interrupt, 0 turns it off. When LCR.DLAB is 1, bit 7 of DLH.

fields.name: DLH6_5
fields.text: When LCR.DLAB is 1, bits 6:5 of DLH.

fields.name: ELCOLR_DLH4
fields.text: IER.ELCOLR (read only), how LSR's overrun, parity and framing error bits and its break interrupt bit are cleared: 0, they clear on a read of the RX FIFO (RBR) or of LSR. When LCR.DLAB is 1, bit 4 of DLH.

fields.name: EDSSI_DLH3
fields.text: IER.EDSSI, modem status interrupt enable (fourth-highest priority): 1 enables it, 0 disables it. When LCR.DLAB is 1, bit 3 of DLH.

fields.name: ELSI_DLH2
fields.text: IER.ELSI, receiver line status interrupt enable (the highest-priority interrupt): 1 enables it, 0 disables it. When LCR.DLAB is 1, bit 2 of DLH.

fields.name: ETBEI_DLH1
fields.text: IER.ETBEI, transmit holding register empty interrupt enable (third-highest priority): 1 enables it, 0 disables it. When LCR.DLAB is 1, bit 1 of DLH.

fields.name: ERBFI_DLH0
fields.text: IER.ERBFI, received data available interrupt enable, which also covers the character timeout interrupt in FIFO mode with FIFOs on (second-highest priority): 1 enables them, 0 disables them. When LCR.DLAB is 1, bit 0 of DLH.

fields.name: IIR_FCR
fields.text: Read: IIR. Bits 7:6 FIFOSE show whether the FIFOs are on (00 off, 11 on); bits 5:4 reserved; bits 3:0 IID give the highest-priority pending interrupt: 0001 none, 0010 THR empty, 0100 RX data available, 0110 RX line status, 0111 busy detect, 1100 character timeout. Write: FCR. Bits 7:6 RT set the RX FIFO level that raises the received data available interrupt, deasserts rts_n under auto flow control, and in some modes asserts dma_rx_req_n: 00 one character, 01 quarter full, 10 half full, 11 two short of full. Bits 5:4 TET set the TX FIFO empty level that raises the THRE interrupt while that mode is on, and in some modes asserts dma_tx_req_n: 00 empty, 01 two characters, 10 quarter full, 11 half full. Bit 3 DMAM picks DMA signalling mode 0 or 1 for the dma_rx_req_n and dma_tx_req_n outputs. Bit 2 XFIFOR resets the TX FIFO control logic and treats the FIFO as empty; bit 1 RFIFOR does the same for the RX FIFO; both clear themselves. Bit 0 FIFOE turns the TX and RX FIFOs on (1) or off (0); any change of it resets the control logic of both FIFOs.

fields.name: UART_DLAB
fields.text: Divisor latch access: 1 gives read and write access to DLL and DLH for setting the baud rate; clear it after the baud rate is set to reach the other registers.

fields.name: UART_BC
fields.text: Break control: 1 sends a break, forcing the serial output to the spacing state (logic 0); outside loopback mode (MCR[4]) sout stays low until this bit is cleared.

fields.name: UART_SP
fields.text: Stick parity, writable only while USR[0] is 0 (UART not busy): forces the parity bit. With PEN, EPS and this bit all 1, parity is sent and checked as logic 0; with PEN and this bit 1 and EPS 0, as logic 1. 0 turns stick parity off.

fields.name: UART_EPS
fields.text: Even parity select, writable only while USR[0] is 0 (UART not busy); applies when LCR.PEN is 1. 1: an even number of logic 1s is sent and checked. 0: an odd number.

fields.name: UART_PEN
fields.text: Parity enable, writable only while USR[0] is 0 (UART not busy): 1 generates parity on sent characters and checks it on received ones, 0 turns parity off.

fields.name: UART_STOP
fields.text: Number of stop bits sent and received per character: 0 gives one stop bit; 1 gives one and a half when LCR[1:0] (DLS) is 0 (5 data bits), else two. Whatever the setting, only the first stop bit is checked on receive.

fields.name: UART_DLS
fields.text: Data length select, the data bits per character sent and received: 00 five, 01 six, 10 seven, 11 eight.

fields.name: UART_AFCE
fields.text: Auto flow control enable: with FIFOs on, 1 turns on the auto flow control features, 0 turns them off.

fields.name: UART_LB
fields.text: Loopback, a diagnostic test mode; all interrupts keep working. sout is held high and the serial output is looped back to sin internally; dsr_n, cts_n, ri_n and dcd_n are cut off, and dtr_n and rts_n feed the modem inputs internally.

fields.name: UART_RTS
fields.text: Request to send: drives the rts_n output, which tells the modem or data set the UART is ready to exchange data. Without auto flow control (MCR[5]=0), writing 1 drives rts_n low and writing 0 de-asserts it. With auto flow control (MCR[5]=1) and FIFOs on (FCR[0]=1), rts_n follows this bit gated by the RX FIFO threshold (inactive high above it). In loopback mode (MCR[4]=1) rts_n is held inactive high and this bit loops back internally to an input.

fields.name: UART_ADDR_RCVD
fields.text: Address received, used with 9-bit data mode (LCR_EXT[0]=1): 1 when the received character's 9th bit is 1, marking it an address; 0 marks it data. In FIFO mode it shows when that character reaches the head of the FIFO. An LSR read clears it; it must be cleared before the next address byte arrives, or software cannot tell successive address interrupts apart.

fields.name: UART_RFE
fields.text: Receiver FIFO error, meaningful only with FIFOs on (FCR[0]=1): 1 when the RX FIFO holds one or more characters with a parity error, a framing error or a break, 0 when none. Cleared by an LSR read once the erroneous character is at the head of the RX FIFO and no later errors are in it.

fields.name: UART_TEMT
fields.text: Transmitter empty: with FIFOs on (FCR[0]=1), set once the TX FIFO and the shift register hold nothing; with FIFOs off, set once THR and the shift register hold nothing.

fields.name: UART_THRE
fields.text: Transmit holding register empty. With THRE mode off (IER[7]=0), with or without FIFOs, set when THR or the TX FIFO is empty: it sets when data moves from THR or the TX FIFO into the transmitter shift register and nothing new has been written, and raises the THRE interrupt if that is enabled. With both THRE mode and FIFOs on (IER[7]=1, FCR[0]=1) it instead shows the TX FIFO is full and no longer drives the THRE interrupt, which then follows the FCR[5:4] threshold.

fields.name: UART_BI
fields.text: Break interrupt: in UART mode (SIR_MODE disabled), set when sin is held at logic 0 longer than start + data + parity + stop bit times. In FIFO mode the break character passes through the FIFO and the bit shows when that character reaches the top. In non-FIFO mode it shows at once and stays until LSR is read. A read of LSR clears it.

fields.name: UART_FE
fields.text: Framing error: 1 when the receiver finds no valid stop bit, 0 otherwise. In FIFO mode it shows when the offending character reaches the head of the FIFO. After a framing error the UART resynchronises by taking the error to be the next character's start bit and then receiving its data, parity and stop bits. It is also set when a break interrupt occurs (LSR[4], BI). An LSR read clears it.

fields.name: UART_PE
fields.text: Parity error: 1 when a received character fails parity while LCR[3] (PEN) is 1, 0 otherwise. In FIFO mode it shows when the offending character reaches the head of the FIFO. It is also set when a break interrupt occurs (LSR[4], BI). An LSR read clears it.

fields.name: UART_OE
fields.text: Overrun error: 1 when a character arrives before the previous one was read, 0 otherwise. Without FIFOs the new character overwrites the one in RBR; in FIFO mode it arrives while the FIFO is full, the FIFO keeps its contents and the character in the receive shift register is lost. An LSR read clears it.

fields.name: UART_DR
fields.text: Data ready: 1 while RBR or the RX FIFO holds at least one character, 0 when none. Cleared by reading RBR without FIFOs, or when the RX FIFO empties in FIFO mode.

fields.name: UART_CTS
fields.text: Clear to send, the inverse of the cts_n input: 1 when cts_n is asserted (logic 0), meaning the modem or data set can exchange data with the UART; 0 when it is deasserted (logic 1). In loopback mode (MCR[4]=1) it equals MCR[1] (RTS).

fields.name: UART_DCTS
fields.text: Delta clear to send: 1 when cts_n has changed since MSR was last read, 0 when not. An MSR read clears it. In loopback mode (MCR[4]=1) it follows changes of MCR[1] (RTS). If it is 0 and cts_n is asserted (low) through a reset of any kind, it is set when the reset ends while cts_n stays asserted.

fields.name: ISO7816_SCRATCH_PAD
fields.text: Scratch bits for software; the UART does nothing with them.

fields.name: ISO7816_ENABLE
fields.text: ISO7816 enable.

fields.name: ISO7816_ERR_SIG_EN
fields.text: ISO7816 error signal enable.

fields.name: ISO7816_CONVENTION
fields.text: ISO7816 convention.

fields.name: SRBR_STHRx
fields.text: Shadow of RBR (read) and THR (write), one of sixteen 32-bit addresses for burst access by the master. Read: the byte received on sin (UART mode) or sir_in (infrared mode), valid only while LSR.DR is 1; with FIFOs off (FCR[0]=0) it must be read before the next byte arrives or it is overwritten and an overrun error results; with FIFOs on (FCR[0]=1) it reads the head of the RX FIFO, and a byte arriving while that FIFO is full is lost, the FIFO contents kept, with an overrun error. Write: the byte to send on sout (UART mode) or sir_out_n (infrared mode), to be written only while LSR[5] (THRE) is 1; with FIFOs off one write clears THRE and further writes before THRE sets again overwrite it; with FIFOs on and THRE set, characters up to the configured FIFO depth (16 by default) may be written, and a write to a full FIFO is lost.

fields.name: UART_RFF
fields.text: Receive FIFO full: 1 when the RX FIFO is completely full, 0 otherwise; clears once the RX FIFO is no longer full.

fields.name: UART_RFNE
fields.text: Receive FIFO not empty: 1 when the RX FIFO holds one or more entries, 0 when it is empty; clears when the RX FIFO empties.

fields.name: UART_TFE
fields.text: Transmit FIFO empty: 1 when the TX FIFO is completely empty, 0 otherwise; clears once the TX FIFO is no longer empty.

fields.name: UART_TFNF
fields.text: Transmit FIFO not full: 1 when the TX FIFO has room, 0 when it is full; clears when the TX FIFO fills.

fields.name: UART_BUSY
fields.text: UART busy: 1 while a serial transfer is in progress, 0 when the UART is idle. It can read 0 while a new character's start bit has just arrived from another device, with THR and RBR empty and no transmission running, since a start bit is recognized only at mid-bit, a delay set by the baud divisor; with a second system clock (CLOCK_MODE enabled) setting the bit also lags by several cycles of the slower clock.

fields.name: UART_TRANSMIT_FIFO_LEVEL
fields.text: Number of entries in the TX FIFO.

fields.name: UART_RECEIVE_FIFO_LEVEL
fields.text: Number of entries in the RX FIFO.

fields.name: UART_XFR
fields.text: TX FIFO reset, a shadow of FCR[2] so the transmit FIFO can be reset without keeping the last FCR value: resets the FIFO's control logic and treats it as empty. Clears itself.

fields.name: UART_RFR
fields.text: RX FIFO reset, a shadow of FCR[1] so the receive FIFO can be reset without keeping the last FCR value: resets the FIFO's control logic and treats it as empty. Clears itself.

fields.name: UART_UR
fields.text: UART reset: resets the UART asynchronously and releases the reset synchronously; with two clocks, both the pclk and sclk domains are reset.

fields.name: UART_SHADOW_REQUEST_TO_SEND
fields.text: Shadow of the RTS bit MCR[1], writable without a read-modify-write of MCR: drives rts_n, which tells the modem or data set the UART is ready to exchange data. Without auto flow control (MCR[5]=0), writing 1 drives rts_n low. With auto flow control (MCR[5]=1) and FIFOs on (FCR[0]=1), rts_n follows the bit gated by the RX FIFO threshold (inactive high above it). In loopback mode (MCR[4]=1) rts_n is held inactive high and the bit loops back internally to an input.

fields.name: UART_SHADOW_BREAK_CONTROL
fields.text: Shadow of the break bit LCR[6], writable without a read-modify-write of LCR: 1 sends a break, forcing the serial output to the spacing state (logic 0); outside loopback mode (MCR[4]) sout stays low until the bit is cleared.

fields.name: UART_SHADOW_DMA_MODE
fields.text: Shadow DMA mode, a separate copy of FCR[3] (DMAM) that can be written alone, without keeping and masking the last FCR value. Picks DMA signalling mode for the dma_rx_req_n and dma_tx_req_n outputs: 0 mode 0, 1 mode 1.

fields.name: UART_SHADOW_FIFO_ENABLE
fields.text: Shadow of the FIFO enable bit FCR[0], writable without keeping and masking the last FCR value: turns the TX and RX FIFOs on or off. Clearing it after they were on resets the controller part of both FIFOs.

fields.name: UART_SHADOW_RCVR_TRIGGER
fields.text: Shadow RCVR trigger, a separate copy of FCR[7:6] that can be written alone, without keeping and masking the last FCR value. Sets the RX FIFO level that raises the received data available interrupt, and that asserts dma_rx_req_n when FCR[3] (DMA mode) is 1: 00 one character, 01 quarter full, 10 half full, 11 two short of full.

fields.name: UART_SHADOW_TX_EMPTY_TRIGGER
fields.text: Shadow TX empty trigger, a separate copy of FCR[5:4] that can be written alone, without keeping and masking the last FCR value. Sets the TX FIFO empty level that raises the THRE interrupt while that mode is on: 00 empty, 01 two characters, 10 quarter full, 11 half full.

fields.name: UART_HALT_TX
fields.text: Halt TX: 1 stops transmission so the master can fill the TX FIFO, 0 lets it run. Applies when FIFOs are implemented and on; with FIFOs off it has no effect.

fields.name: UART_DMASA
fields.text: DMA software acknowledge, for ending a transfer on an error, such as the DMA disabling the channel: the UART de-asserts its request and single signals for both TX and RX. Clears itself.

fields.name: UART_DLF
fields.text: Fractional part of the baud divisor, added to the integer divisor in DLH and DLL; worth UART_DLF/16.

fields.name: UART_RAR
fields.text: Receive address to match: when a character arrives with its 9th bit set, its lower 8 bits are compared with this value; on a match, following characters with the 9th bit 0 are taken as data until the next address byte. Used only with LCR_EXT.ADDR_MATCH (LCR_EXT[1]) and LCR_EXT.DLS_E (LCR_EXT[0]) both 1; write it only while the UART is not busy.

fields.name: UART_TAR
fields.text: Transmit address: with LCR_EXT.DLS_E (LCR_EXT[0]) on and LCR_EXT.SEND_ADDR (LCR_EXT[2]) set, the UART sends a 9-bit character with the 9th bit 1 and these 8 bits as the address. Only the address goes here; data is written to THR. SEND_ADDR is cleared by hardware once the address starts going out.

fields.name: UART_TRANSMIT_MODE
fields.text: Transmit mode for 9-bit transfers. 1: THR and STHR are 9 bits wide and each write carries its own 9th bit, 1 for an address and 0 for data; the transmit address register (TAR) is not used. 0: THR and STHR are 8 bits wide; the address goes in TAR, data in THR/STHR, and SEND_ADDR says when the address is sent.

fields.name: UART_SEND_ADDR
fields.text: Send address, the trigger for sending the address while transmitting. 1: a 9-bit character goes out with the 9th bit 1 and the other 8 bits from the transmit address register. 0: 9-bit characters go out with the 9th bit 0 and the other 8 bits from the TX FIFO, written through the 8-bit THR/STHR. Hardware clears it after the address character is sent; it is not to be written 0. Applies only when DLS_E is 1 and TRANSMIT_MODE is 0.

fields.name: UART_ADDR_MATCH
fields.text: Address match mode for receive, applies only when DLS_E is 1. 1: the UART waits for a character with its 9th bit 1 and compares it with the receive address match register; on a match the characters that follow are taken as data and received. 0: normal mode; every 9-bit character is received into the RX FIFO, and software reads it and tells address from data.

fields.name: UART_DLS_E
fields.text: DLS extension: turns on 9-bit data for transmit and receive.

fields.name: ISO7816_AUTO_GT
fields.text: ISO7816 automatic guard time: 0 sends as soon as TX data is ready, 1 sends each new character after the guard time.

values.text: Sends as soon as TX data is ready.
Sends each new character after the guard time.

fields.name: ISO7816_ERR_TX_VALUE_IRQMASK
fields.text: ISO7816 ERR_TX_VALUE interrupt mask.

fields.name: ISO7816_ERR_TX_TIME_IRQMASK
fields.text: ISO7816 ERR_TX_TIME interrupt mask.

fields.name: ISO7816_TIM_EXPIRED_IRQMASK
fields.text: ISO7816 timer expired interrupt mask: 0 masks the interrupt, 1 enables it.

fields.name: ISO7816_CLK_STATUS
fields.text: ISO7816 clock status.

fields.name: ISO7816_CLK_LEVEL
fields.text: Level of the ISO7816 clock while stopped: 0 low, 1 high.

fields.name: ISO7816_CLK_EN
fields.text: ISO7816 clock enable.

fields.name: ISO7816_CLK_DIV
fields.text: ISO7816 clock divider: ISO7816 clock = sclk / (2 x (ISO7816_CLK_DIV + 1)).

fields.name: ISO7816_TIM_MODE
fields.text: ISO7816 timer mode. 0: the timer, clocked by the ISO7816 clock, counts up to its maximum and stops; it is restarted by disabling and re-enabling it. 1: the timer counts guard time, with ISO7816_TIM_MAX set to 16 x guard time - 1.

values.text: Counts up to the maximum and stops; disable and re-enable the timer to restart it. Clocked by the ISO7816 clock.
Counts the guard time; ISO7816_TIM_MAX must be 16 x guard time - 1.

fields.name: ISO7816_TIM_EN
fields.text: ISO7816 timer enable.

fields.name: ISO7816_TIM_MAX
fields.text: Write: the value the timer counts up to from 0. Read: the timer's present count.

fields.name: ISO7816_ERR_PULSE_WIDTH
fields.text: Width of the error signal in 1/16 etu, with the error signal on and receiving.

fields.name: ISO7816_ERR_PULSE_OFFSET
fields.text: Offset of the error signal from 9.6 etu, in 1/16 etu, with the error signal on and receiving.

fields.name: ISO7816_ERR_TX_VALUE_IRQ
fields.text: ISO7816 TX value error interrupt. Read 1: with the error signal enabled in transmit mode, the receiver did not take the character correctly. Write 1 clears it.

fields.name: ISO7816_ERR_TX_TIME_IRQ
fields.text: ISO7816 TX time error interrupt. Read 1: with the error signal enabled in transmit mode, raised when the module checks the error signal. Write 1 clears it.

fields.name: ISO7816_TIM_EXPIRED_IRQ
fields.text: ISO7816 timer expired interrupt: reads 1 when the timer has expired. Disabling the timer clears it; when sclk is slower than pclk, the bit must be checked as cleared before the interrupt handler returns.

fields.name: UART_UCV
fields.text: Component version.

fields.name: UART_CTR
fields.text: Component type.

fields.name: LSMODE
fields.text: Low-speed mode: 1 runs the node at USB low speed (1.5 Mbit/s), moves the pull-up from D+ to D- and sets D+/D- edge times to the USB low-speed values. Change it only while USBEN is 0.

fields.name: USB_NAT
fields.text: Node attached: 1 lets the hub see this node as attached and stops the node driving the bus, so it must then be able to take a bus reset; 0 makes the transceiver hold SE0 so no attach is seen. Cleared by reset and while the node is disabled; can be set only when USBEN is 1.

fields.name: USB_DBG
fields.text: Debug mode: 1 makes MAEV, ALTEV, NAKEV and the transmit and receive status registers writable and puts the node in a locked state; node states are then readable in XCVDIAG with UTR.DIAG set. Clear-on-read bits keep working. Can be set only when USBEN is 1.

fields.name: USBEN
fields.text: USB enable: 1 turns the full/low-speed node on. 0 turns it off, stops its 48 MHz clock, returns every USB register to its reset value and makes the transceiver hold SE0 so the hub does not see the node. 0 after reset.

fields.name: USB_VPIN
fields.text: When bit 0 is 1, reads the USB_Dp receive level from the transceiver (D+ against VSE).

fields.name: USB_VMIN
fields.text: When bit 0 is 1, reads the USB_Dm receive level from the transceiver (D- against VSE).

fields.name: USB_RCV
fields.text: When bit 0 is 1, reads the output of the differential receive comparator.

fields.name: USB_XCV_TXEN
fields.text: When bit 0 is 1, enables test bits 2 and 1. Keep at 0 in normal use.

fields.name: USB_XCV_TXn
fields.text: When bits 3 and 0 are 1, drives USB_Dm high whatever LSMODE is.

fields.name: USB_XCV_TXp
fields.text: When bits 3 and 0 are 1, drives USB_Dp high whatever LSMODE is.

fields.name: USB_XCV_TEST
fields.text: Turns on the test bits of USB_XCVDIAG_REG. 0: normal operation, test bits off; 1: bits 7, 6, 5, 3, 2 and 1 take effect.

fields.name: USB_VADJ
fields.text: Sets the threshold voltage of the single-ended receivers. Leave unchanged unless Dialog says otherwise; active only when USB_UTR_REG[7] is 1.

fields.name: USB_CADJ
fields.text: Sets the current that controls the driver edge rate. Leave unchanged unless Dialog says otherwise; active only when USB_UTR_REG[7] is 1.

fields.name: USB_DIAG
fields.text: Diagnostic enable: 0 for normal use; 1 opens access to USB_XCVDIAG_REG and USB_TCR_REG. Diagnostic use only.

fields.name: USB_NCRC
fields.text: No CRC16: 1 sends every packet from the node without its trailing CRC16, so other nodes' CRC error detection can be checked; reception is not affected. Diagnostic use only.

fields.name: USB_SF
fields.text: Short frame: 1 lets the frame timer lock to and follow short frame lengths outside the USB specification. Keep at 0 in normal use; test use only.

fields.name: USB_UTR_RES
fields.text: Reserved; keep at 0.

fields.name: USB_AD_EN
fields.text: Address enable: 1 compares tokens against the address in bits 6-0; 0 makes the device ignore every token on the bus. With EPC0.DEF set, endpoint 0 still answers the default address.

fields.name: USB_AD
fields.text: The 7-bit function address of this device, used for every token it sends and receives.

fields.name: USB_NFS
fields.text: Node functional state, read and written to follow and set the USB node's state. 00 NodeReset: the USB reset state, entered on a module reset or by software when a USB reset is seen; all endpoint pipes are off on entry, software clears EPC0.DEF and FAR.AD_EN on entry and resets DEF on exit so the node answers the default address. 01 NodeResume: the node drives resume signalling; firmware enters it to start a remote wake-up and holds it 1 ms to 15 ms. 10 NodeOperational: normal state, node set up for the bus. 11 NodeSuspend: firmware enters it from Operational when a suspend is seen; the transceivers go to low-power suspend, every endpoint controller is reset, as are RX_EN, TX_EN and LAST, and other internal state is held; bus activity sets ALTEV.RESUME, after which software can return to NodeOperational.

fields.name: USB_CH_EV
fields.text: Charger event: set when any of USB_CHARGER_STAT_REG bits 2-0 changes; cleared by reading USB_CHARGER_STAT_REG.

fields.name: USB_EP0_NAK
fields.text: Endpoint 0 NAK event: 1 when either EP0_NAK_REG.EP0_OUTNAK or EP0_NAK_REG.EP0_INNAK is 1; cleared by reading EP0_NAK_REG.

fields.name: USB_EP0_RX
fields.text: Endpoint 0 receive event: copy of RXS0.RX_LAST, cleared by reading RXS0. FIFO0 cannot overrun, as endpoint 0 stores a whole packet before passing it on.

fields.name: USB_EP0_TX
fields.text: Endpoint 0 transmit event: copy of TXS0.TX_DONE, cleared by reading TXS0. FIFO0 cannot underrun, as endpoint 0 stores a whole packet before passing it on.

fields.name: USB_INTR
fields.text: Master interrupt enable: always 0 in MAEV; the enable itself is bit 7 of MAMSK.

fields.name: USB_RX_EV
fields.text: Receive event: set when any unmasked RXEV bit is 1, meaning a SETUP or OUT transaction has finished. Clears when every RXSn.RX_LAST bit and every RXEV.RXOVRRN bit is 0.

fields.name: USB_ULD
fields.text: Unlocked/locked detected: set when the frame timer goes from locked to unlocked or back to locked, as FNH.UL shows; cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_NAK
fields.text: NAK event: set when an unmasked NAKEV bit becomes 1; cleared by reading NAKEV.

fields.name: USB_FRAME
fields.text: Frame event: set when the frame counter takes a new value, from a valid SOF or from an artificial step when the counter is unlocked or a frame was missed; cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_TX_EV
fields.text: Transmit event: set when any unmasked TXEV bit (TXFIFOn or TXUNDRNn) is 1, meaning an IN transaction has finished. Clears when every TXSn.TX_DONE and TXUNDRN bit is 0.

fields.name: USB_ALT
fields.text: Alternate event: set when an unmasked ALTEV bit becomes 1; cleared by reading ALTEV.

fields.name: USB_WARN
fields.text: Warning event: set when an unmasked FWEV bit becomes 1; cleared by reading FWEV.

fields.name: USB_M_CH_EV
fields.text: Mask for MAEV.USB_CH_EV. In MAMSK, 1 lets the matching MAEV event raise an interrupt and 0 stops it.

fields.name: USB_M_EP0_NAK
fields.text: Mask for MAEV.USB_EP0_NAK: 1 lets it raise an interrupt.

fields.name: USB_M_EP0_RX
fields.text: Mask for MAEV.USB_EP0_RX: 1 lets it raise an interrupt.

fields.name: USB_M_EP0_TX
fields.text: Mask for MAEV.USB_EP0_TX: 1 lets it raise an interrupt.

fields.name: USB_M_INTR
fields.text: Master interrupt enable for the MAEV events.

fields.name: USB_M_RX_EV
fields.text: Mask for MAEV.USB_RX_EV: 1 lets it raise an interrupt.

fields.name: USB_M_ULD
fields.text: Mask for MAEV.USB_ULD: 1 lets it raise an interrupt.

fields.name: USB_M_NAK
fields.text: Mask for MAEV.USB_NAK: 1 lets it raise an interrupt.

fields.name: USB_M_FRAME
fields.text: Mask for MAEV.USB_FRAME: 1 lets it raise an interrupt.

fields.name: USB_M_TX_EV
fields.text: Mask for MAEV.USB_TX_EV: 1 lets it raise an interrupt.

fields.name: USB_M_ALT
fields.text: Mask for MAEV.USB_ALT: 1 lets it raise an interrupt.

fields.name: USB_M_WARN
fields.text: Mask for MAEV.USB_WARN: 1 lets it raise an interrupt.

fields.name: USB_RESUME
fields.text: Resume: set when, with NFSR.NFS in suspend, a non-idle state appears on the bus, telling the device to wake up and go to the operational state. Cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_RESET
fields.text: Reset: set after 2.5 us of SE0 on the upstream port. Software then puts NFSR.NFS in reset for at least 100 us before returning to operational. Cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_SD5
fields.text: Suspend detect 5 ms: set after 5 ms of idle on the upstream port; the device may then do a remote wake-up, started by firmware writing resume to NFSR. Cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_SD3
fields.text: Suspend detect 3 ms: set after 3 ms of idle on the upstream port, meaning the device should suspend; firmware does it by writing suspend to NFSR. Cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_EOP
fields.text: End of packet: a valid EOP was seen on the bus; after a remote wake-up started by this device, it shows the host has acknowledged and finished the resume. Cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_M_RESUME
fields.text: Mask for ALTEV.USB_RESUME. In ALTMSK, 1 lets the matching ALTEV event set MAEV.ALT and 0 stops it.

fields.name: USB_M_RESET
fields.text: Mask for ALTEV.USB_RESET: 1 lets it set MAEV.ALT.

fields.name: USB_M_SD5
fields.text: Mask for ALTEV.USB_SD5: 1 lets it set MAEV.ALT.

fields.name: USB_M_SD3
fields.text: Mask for ALTEV.USB_SD3: 1 lets it set MAEV.ALT.

fields.name: USB_M_EOP
fields.text: Mask for ALTEV.USB_EOP: 1 lets it set MAEV.ALT.

fields.name: USB_TXUDRRN31
fields.text: Transmit underrun for endpoints 3:1: each bit copies TX_URUN of its TXSn and goes to 1 when that transmit FIFO underflows; cleared by reading that TXSn.

fields.name: USB_TXFIFO31
fields.text: Transmit FIFO for endpoints 3:1: each bit copies TX_DONE of its TXSn and goes to 1 when that endpoint's IN transaction finishes; cleared by reading that TXSn.

fields.name: USB_M_TXUDRRN31
fields.text: Masks for TXEV.USB_TXUDRRN31: a bit at 1 lets the matching TXEV bit set MAEV.TX_EV; at 0 it does not.

fields.name: USB_M_TXFIFO31
fields.text: Masks for TXEV.USB_TXFIFO31: a bit at 1 lets the matching TXEV bit set MAEV.TX_EV; at 0 it does not.

fields.name: USB_RXOVRRN31
fields.text: Receive overrun for FIFOs 3:1: a bit goes to 1 when its receive FIFO overruns; cleared by reading the register. For the streaming receive endpoints EP2, EP4 and EP6, whose packets can be longer than the FIFO, firmware checks RX_ERR to find packets corrupted by errors.

fields.name: USB_RXFIFO31
fields.text: Receive FIFO for endpoints 3:1: a bit goes to 1 when RX_ERR or RX_LAST of its RXSn is 1, and clears when that RXSn is read; clear-on-read is off while Freeze is asserted. Endpoint 0 packets with errors are dropped, so a retransmitted SETUP is captured cleanly. With streaming on EP2, EP4, EP6 or EP8, firmware checks RX_ERR.

fields.name: USB_M_RXOVRRN31
fields.text: Masks for RXEV.USB_RXOVRRN31: a bit at 1 lets the matching RXEV bit set MAEV.RX_EV; at 0 it does not.

fields.name: USB_M_RXFIFO31
fields.text: Masks for RXEV.USB_RXFIFO31: a bit at 1 lets the matching RXEV bit set MAEV.RX_EV; at 0 it does not.

fields.name: USB_OUT31
fields.text: OUT NAK for endpoints 3:1: a bit goes to 1 when a NAK answers an OUT token to an enabled address and endpoint (FAR.AD_EN and EPCx.EP_EN both 1), but not for a NAK caused by overrun. Cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_IN31
fields.text: IN NAK for endpoints 3:1: a bit goes to 1 when a NAK answers an IN token to an enabled address and endpoint (FAR.AD_EN and EPCx.EP_EN both 1). Cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_M_OUT31
fields.text: Masks for NAKEV.USB_OUT31: a bit at 1 lets the matching NAKEV bit set MAEV.NAK; at 0 it does not.

fields.name: USB_M_IN31
fields.text: Masks for NAKEV.USB_IN31: a bit at 1 lets the matching NAKEV bit set MAEV.NAK; at 0 it does not.

fields.name: USB_RXWARN31
fields.text: Receive warning for endpoints 3:1: a bit goes to 1 when its receive FIFO reaches the limit set by EPCx RFWL; it clears when data is read from the FIFO or the FIFO is flushed.

fields.name: USB_TXWARN31
fields.text: Transmit warning for endpoints 3:1: a bit goes to 1 when its transmit FIFO reaches the limit set by TXCn.TFWL while transmission is enabled; it clears when new data is written, the FIFO is flushed, or TXSn.TX_DONE shows the transmission done.

fields.name: USB_M_RXWARN31
fields.text: Masks for FWEV.USB_RXWARN31: a bit at 1 lets the matching FWEV bit set MAEV.WARN; at 0 it does not.

fields.name: USB_M_TXWARN31
fields.text: Masks for FWEV.USB_TXWARN31: a bit at 1 lets the matching FWEV bit set MAEV.WARN; at 0 it does not.

fields.name: USB_MF
fields.text: Missed SOF flag: set by hardware when a valid SOF carries a frame number other than the expected next one, or no SOF arrives within 12060 bit times. Cleared by reading FNH.

fields.name: USB_UL
fields.text: Unlock flag: set by hardware when two or more frames arrive without the expected frame number, or no valid SOF arrives within 12060 bit times; while set, FN is loaded from the next valid SOF. Cleared by reading FNH.

fields.name: USB_RFC
fields.text: Reset frame count: writing 1 sets the frame number to 0x000 and the bit then returns to 0. Always reads 0.

fields.name: USB_FN_10_8
fields.text: Bits 10:8 of the frame number from the last SOF. With no valid frame number within 12060 bit times (FLMAX with tolerance), the number steps on by itself; after two missed or wrong frames it holds and takes the next valid SOF's number. After FNL is read, FNH gives the bits latched at that read; read FNL first, then FNH. Reading FNH without FNL first gives the live bits.

fields.name: USB_FN
fields.text: Low byte of the frame number. Reading it latches the three frame number bits of FNH until FNH is read; read FNL first, then FNH.

fields.name: RPU_TEST7
fields.text: Test bit.

fields.name: RPU_TEST_SW2
fields.text: Test control of switch SW2, the reduced pull-up on USB_Dp and USB_Dm; 1 opens it whatever the VBus state.

values.text: SW2 closed: reduced pull-up connected to USB_Dp and USB_Dm.
SW2 open, whatever the VBus state.

fields.name: RPU_TEST_SW1
fields.text: Test control of switch SW1, the USB_Dp pull-up; 0 closes it, 1 opens it whatever the VBus state.

values.text: SW1 open: USB_Dp pull-up off, whatever the VBus state.

fields.name: RPU_TEST_EN
fields.text: Pull-up resistor test enable. 0: normal operation; 1: RPU_TEST_SW1, RPU_TEST_SW1DM and RPU_TEST_SW2 take effect.

fields.name: RPU_TEST_SW1DM
fields.text: Test control of switch SW1DM, the USB_Dm pull-up; 0 closes it, 1 opens it whatever the VBus state.

values.text: SW1DM open: USB_Dm pull-up off, whatever the VBus state.

fields.name: RPU_RCDELAY
fields.text: Test bit; keep at 0.

fields.name: RPU_SSPROTEN
fields.text: Test bit; keep at 0.

fields.name: USB_STALL
fields.text: Stall: 1 makes the endpoint answer with STALL when an IN token arrives with the transmit FIFO enabled or an OUT token arrives with the receive FIFO enabled; a SETUP token never gets a STALL. Sending the STALL sets RX_LAST and TX_DONE in the receive and transmit status registers.

fields.name: USB_DEF
fields.text: Default address: 1 makes the device answer the default address whatever FAR6-0 and EP03-0 hold; hardware clears it when an IN packet for the endpoint is sent. The address may not change before the SET_ADDRESS control sequence has finished, and must change right after it. On a bus reset firmware has 10 ms to write 0x80 to FAR and 0x00 to EPC0; on SET_ADDRESS it writes 0x40 to EPC0 and 0x80 or the assigned address to FAR, then queues a zero-length IN packet for the status phase.

fields.name: USB_EP
fields.text: Endpoint address; fixed at 0000b for endpoint 0, and writes of 1 to it have no effect.

fields.name: USB_TXFD
fields.text: Transmit FIFO data byte. Firmware writes the payload only; the PID and CRC16 are added by hardware.

fields.name: USB_ACK_STAT
fields.text: Acknowledge status: valid when TX_DONE is 1. 1 means the host acknowledged the last packet sent; otherwise 0. Cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_TX_DONE
fields.text: Transmission done: 1 means a packet has finished sending. Cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_TCOUNT
fields.text: Transmission count: free bytes in the FIFO; at most 8 for endpoint 0.

fields.name: USB_IGN_IN
fields.text: Ignore IN tokens: 1 makes the endpoint ignore IN tokens sent to its address.

fields.name: USB_FLUSH
fields.text: Flush FIFO: writing 1 empties the control endpoint FIFOs, returns the endpoint to idle, resets the FIFO read and write pointers and then clears itself. If FIFO0 is in a bus transfer, the flush waits until it ends. Same as RXC0.FLUSH.

fields.name: USB_TOGGLE_TX0
fields.text: Toggle: PID of the packet sent, 0 for DATA0 and 1 for DATA1. Hardware never changes it.

fields.name: USB_TX_EN
fields.text: Transmission enable: firmware sets it to send from the FIFO; hardware clears it after one packet or a STALL sent for an IN token. RXC0.RX_EN wins: while RX_EN is set, TX_EN is ignored. Setting it with nothing in the FIFO sends a zero-length packet.

fields.name: USB_EP0_OUTNAK
fields.text: Endpoint 0 OUT NAK: goes to 1 when a NAK answers an OUT token to an enabled address (FAR.AD_EN 1), but not for a NAK caused by overrun. Cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_EP0_INNAK
fields.text: Endpoint 0 IN NAK: goes to 1 when a NAK answers an IN token to an enabled address (FAR.AD_EN 1). Cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_RXFD
fields.text: Receive FIFO data byte. Firmware reads the payload only; the PID and CRC16 are stripped by hardware. Readable and writable in TEST mode.

fields.name: USB_SETUP
fields.text: Setup: 1 means a SETUP packet was received. Left as is by zero-length packets; cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_TOGGLE_RX0
fields.text: Toggle: PID of the last packet received correctly, 0 for DATA0 and 1 for DATA1. Left as is by zero-length packets; cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_RX_LAST
fields.text: Receive last: 1 means an ACK was sent at the end of a successful receive. Left as is by zero-length packets; cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_RCOUNT
fields.text: Receive count: bytes now in the receive FIFO; at most 8 for endpoint 0.

fields.name: USB_FLUSH
fields.text: Flush: writing 1 empties the control endpoint FIFOs, returns the endpoint to idle, resets the FIFO read and write pointers and then clears itself. If FIFO0 is in a bus transfer, the flush waits until it ends. 0 after reset. Same as TXC0.FLUSH.

fields.name: USB_IGN_SETUP
fields.text: Ignore SETUP tokens: 1 makes the endpoint ignore SETUP tokens sent to its address.

fields.name: USB_IGN_OUT
fields.text: Ignore OUT tokens: 1 makes the endpoint ignore OUT tokens sent to its address.

fields.name: USB_RX_EN
fields.text: Receive enable: OUT reception turns off after each data packet and after a STALL for an OUT token; write 1 to turn it back on. SETUP packets are always received. A valid SETUP following another SETUP with no other token between is dropped and answered with ACK; a SETUP the controller cannot take for any other reason gets no handshake, so a lost ACK of the first SETUP can be recovered.

fields.name: USB_STALL
fields.text: Stall: 1 makes the endpoint answer with STALL when an IN token arrives with the transmit FIFO enabled or an OUT token arrives with the receive FIFO enabled. A SETUP token never gets a STALL.

fields.name: USB_ISO
fields.text: Isochronous: 1 makes the endpoint isochronous, so it sends no NAK when enabled but not ready (an IN with an empty FIFO, or an OUT with a full FIFO), as isochronous transfers have no handshake.

fields.name: USB_EP_EN
fields.text: Endpoint enable: 1 makes EP[3:0] take part in address matching together with FAR.AD[6:0]; 0 makes the endpoint ignore every token on the bus.

fields.name: USB_EP
fields.text: Endpoint address, 4 bits.

fields.name: USB_TXFD
fields.text: Transmit FIFO data byte. Firmware writes the payload only; the PID and CRC16 are added by hardware. Readable and writable over the core bus in TEST mode.

fields.name: USB_TX_URUN
fields.text: Transmit FIFO underrun: set when the transmit FIFO runs empty during a transmission with no new data written; the MAC then forces a bit-stuff error and an EOP. Cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_ACK_STAT
fields.text: Acknowledge status, valid when TX_DONE is set. Without ISO (EPCx.ISO 0): 1 means the host acknowledged the last packet, otherwise 0. With ISO: 1 means a frame number LSB match (TXCx.IGN_ISOMSK) occurred and data went out for an IN token; otherwise the bit is 0, the FIFO gets flushed and TX_DONE goes to 1. Cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_TX_DONE
fields.text: Transmission done: 1 means the endpoint answered a bus packet: a data packet sent for an IN token without ISO, a STALL sent for an IN token, or a scheduled ISO frame sent or dropped. Cleared by reading the register.

fields.name: USB_TCOUNT
fields.text: Transmission count: free bytes in the FIFO; reads 31 when more than 31 are free.

fields.name: USB_IGN_ISOMSK

fields.name: WDOG_WEN
fields.text: Write enable: the watchdog accepts a write only when these bits are all 0, which guards against a runaway program reloading it.

fields.name: WDOG_VAL_NEG
fields.text: Sign of the watchdog count: 1 when it is negative.

fields.name: WDOG_VAL
fields.text: Watchdog count. A write sets the reload value, taken only when bits 31:14 are all 0; the watchdog picks it up on the second following RC32K or RCX tick. A read gives the running count, which drops by 1 each tick, about 10 ms on RC32K or about 29 ms on RCX (chosen by CLK_RCX_REG.RCX_ENABLE, RC32K by default), going 2, 1, 0, 0x3FFF, 0x3FFE and on, with bit 13 marking negative. With WATCHDOG_CTRL_REG.NMI_RST = 0, 0 gives an NMI and 0x3FF0 a WDOG reset with reload to 0x1FFF, 15 ticks after the NMI; with NMI_RST = 1, a count of 0 or below gives a WDOG reset with reload to 0x1FFF.

fields.name: WRITE_BUSY
fields.text: 1 while a value written to WATCHDOG_REG.WDOG_VAL is still being passed to the watchdog; no new WDOG_VAL can be written until it reads 0.

fields.name: WDOG_FREEZE_EN
fields.text: With NMI_RST = 0, 1 lets SET_FREEZE_REG.FRZ_WDOG and RESET_FREEZE_REG.FRZ_WDOG freeze and resume the watchdog; 0 stops that. The bit keeps its value through sleep but SET_FREEZE_REG.FRZ_SYS_WDOG does not, so the watchdog cannot stay frozen while the CM33 sleeps.

fields.name: NMI_RST
fields.text: Watchdog action. 0: NMI at a count of 0 and WDOG (SYS) reset at -16 or below; the watchdog can be frozen and resumed with SET_FREEZE_REG.FRZ_WDOG and RESET_FREEZE_REG.FRZ_WDOG. 1: WDOG (SYS) reset at 0, and software cannot freeze it. Software can only set the bit; only a WDOG (SYS) reset or software reset clears it. The watchdog is always frozen while the Cortex-M33 is halted in debug.

fields.text: Any write clears the SDADC interrupt (ADC_INT). Reads 0.

fields.name: SDADC_VAL
fields.text: Linear result of the last conversion, up to 16 bits; how many bits are meaningful depends on the OSR.

fields.name: GP_ADC_DIFF_TEMP_EN
fields.text: Temperature sensor enable.

fields.name: GP_ADC_DIFF_TEMP_SEL
fields.text: Differential temperature sensor choice. With the sensors on: 0 GND, 1 sensor near the radio, 2 sensor near the charger, 3 sensor near the bandgap. With GP_ADC_DIFF_TEMP_EN = 0, sensors off: 0 GND, 1 Z (open), 2 the charger's V(ntc), 3 the charger's V(temp).

fields.name: GP_ADC_LDO_ZERO
fields.text: Samples VREF and then disconnects it.

values.text: VREF is sampled and then disconnected; refresh it often. The LDO draws power while this bit is set.

fields.name: GP_ADC_CHOP
fields.text: Chopper mode.

values.text: On: two samples with opposite GP_ADC_SIGN cancel the ADC's internal offset; strongly advised for DC measurements.

fields.name: GP_ADC_SIGN
fields.text: Inverts the sign at the ADC input and output.

values.text: Input and output sign inverted, to cancel the ADC's internal offset.

fields.name: GP_ADC_SEL
fields.text: Input select. Single-ended (GP_ADC_SE = 1): 0 GP ADC0 (P1_09); 1 GP ADC1 (P0_25); 2 GP ADC2 (P0_08); 3 GP ADC3 (P0_09); 4 VDD, internal; 5 and 6 V30, with the GP_ADC_ATTN3X scaler chosen by hardware; 7 reserved; 8 VBAT1 with the 5 V to 1.2 V scaler; 9 VSSA (ground of the analog side); 10-15 reserved; 16 P1_13 (GP ADC4); 17 P1_12 (GP ADC5); 18 P1_18 (GP ADC6); 19 P1_19 (GP ADC7); 20 differential temperature sensor, picked by GP_ADC_DIFF_TEMP_SEL; 21-31 reserved. Differential (GP_ADC_SE = 0): 0 P1[09] against P0[25]; any other value P0[08] against P0[09].

fields.name: GP_ADC_MUTE
fields.text: Mutes the ADC input.

values.text: Input muted: the sample is taken at mid-scale, to find the ADC's internal offset and noise relative to VDD_REF, which the ADC also samples.

fields.name: GP_ADC_SE
fields.text: Single-ended or differential input.

fields.name: GP_ADC_MINT
fields.text: GP ADC interrupt mask.

fields.name: GP_ADC_INT
fields.text: Conversion-done interrupt flag; cleared by any write to GP_ADC_CLEAR_INT_REG.

values.text: Conversion done and interrupt raised; cleared by any write to GP_ADC_CLEAR_INT_REG.

fields.name: GP_ADC_CLK_SEL
fields.text: ADC clock select.

fields.name: GP_ADC_CONT
fields.text: Conversion mode: manual or continuous.

values.text: Manual mode: one result per GP_ADC_START.
Continuous mode: results keep going to GP_ADC_RESULT_REG; GP_ADC_START still starts it, and GP_ADC_INTERVAL sets the time between conversions.

fields.name: GP_ADC_START
fields.text: Writing 1 starts a conversion; the bit returns to 0 when it ends, and GP_ADC_INT is set. Do not write it while it is not yet 0.

fields.name: GP_ADC_EN
fields.text: Turns on the GP ADC: its LDO first, then the ADC.

values.text: LDO turned on, then the ADC enabled.

fields.name: GP_ADC_STORE_DEL
fields.text: When a conversion result is stored, counted from the internal start trigger.

values.text: Two ADC_CLK cycles after the internal start trigger.
Sixteen ADC_CLK cycles after the internal start trigger.

fields.name: GP_ADC_SMPL_TIME
fields.text: Sample time, the time the sampling switch is closed, in ADC_CLK cycles.

fields.name: GP_ADC_CONV_NRS
fields.text: Number of samples taken per conversion.

fields.name: GP_ADC_DMA_EN
fields.text: GP ADC DMA enable.

fields.name: GP_ADC_I20U
fields.text: Adds a constant 20 uA load on the ADC LDO.

values.text: A constant 20 uA load is added on the ADC LDO to reduce ripple on the ADC reference voltage.

fields.name: GP_ADC_IDYN
fields.text: Adds a dynamic load current on the ADC LDO.

values.text: A dynamic load current is applied on the ADC LDO to reduce ripple on the ADC reference voltage.

fields.name: GP_ADC_ATTN3X
fields.text: 3x input attenuator, raising the input range from 1.2 V to 3.6 V.

values.text: 3x attenuator on, inputs up to 3.6 V; set by hardware when ADC_SEL is 7 or 8. Needs a longer sample time.

fields.name: GP_ADC_INTERVAL
fields.text: Time between two conversions while GP_ADC_CONT is set, in steps of 1.024 ms. 0: no extra delay; 1: 1.024 ms; 2: 2.048 ms; up to 255: 261.12 ms.

fields.name: GP_ADC_EN_DEL
fields.text: Delay from turning on the LDO to turning on the ADC: n x 32 ADC_CLK periods, 1 giving 32. 0 is not allowed.

fields.name: GP_ADC_OFFP
fields.text: Offset correction of the positive array of the ADC network; used when GP_ADC_SE is 0, or GP_ADC_SE is 1 with GP_ADC_SIGN 0.

fields.name: GP_ADC_OFFN
fields.text: Offset correction of the negative array of the ADC network; used when GP_ADC_SE is 0, or GP_ADC_SE is 1 with GP_ADC_SIGN 1.

fields.name: GP_ADC_CLR_INT
fields.text: Any write clears the GP ADC interrupt (ADC_INT). Reads 0.

fields.name: GP_ADC_VAL
fields.text: Linear result of the last conversion, 10 to 16 bits. The top 10 bits are always valid; the low 6 only with oversampling: 2 samples add one bit and 64 samples add six.

fields.name: P0_DATA
fields.text: Write sets the P0 output latch; read gives the P0 pin levels.

fields.name: P1_DATA
fields.text: Write sets the P1 output latch; read gives the P1 pin levels.

fields.name: P0_SET
fields.text: A 1 in bit y drives P0[y] high; 0 bits have no effect; reads as 0.

fields.name: P1_SET
fields.text: A 1 in bit y drives P1[y] high; 0 bits have no effect; reads as 0.

fields.name: P0_RESET
fields.text: A 1 in bit y drives P0[y] low; 0 bits have no effect; reads as 0.

fields.name: P1_RESET
fields.text: A 1 in bit y drives P1[y] low; 0 bits have no effect; reads as 0.

fields.name: PPOD
fields.text: Output stage type: push-pull or open-drain.

fields.name: PUPD
fields.text: Pull resistor and direction of the pin when used as GPIO; ignored in ADC mode.

fields.name: PID
fields.text: Selects the pin's function. 0: GPIO, with direction and pulls from PUPD. UART: 1 RX and 2 TX. UART2: 3 RX, 4 TX, 5 CTSN and 6 RTSN. UART3: 7 RX, 8 TX, 9 CTSN and 10 RTSN. ISO: 11 CLK and 12 DATA. SPI: 13 DI, 14 DO, 15 CLK and 16 EN. SPI2: 17 DI, 18 DO, 19 CLK and 20 EN. I2C: 21 SCL and 22 SDA. I2C2: 23 SCL and 24 SDA. 25: USB_SOF. 26: ADC, on its dedicated pins only. 27: USB, on P0_14 and P0_15 only. PCM: 28 DI, 29 DO, 30 FSC and 31 CLK. PDM: 32 DATA and 33 CLK. Coexistence: 34 COEX_EXT_ACT, 35 COEX_SMART_ACT and 36 COEX_SMART_PRI. 37 to 41: PORT0_DCF up to PORT4_DCF. 42: CLOCK, on its dedicated pins, with the clock picked in GPIO_CLK_SEL_REG. 43: PG, dedicated pins only. 44: LCD, dedicated pins only. LCD SPI: 45 DC, 46 DO, 47 CLK and 48 EN. Timers: 49 TIM_PWM, 50 TIM2_PWM, 51 TIM_1SHOT, 52 TIM2_1SHOT, 53 TIM3_PWM and 54 TIM4_PWM. 55: reserved. 56 to 58: CMAC_DIAG0 to CMAC_DIAG2. 59: CMAC_DIAGX, dedicated pins only. 60 to 63: reserved.

fields.name: P0_OUT_CTRL
fields.text: One bit per P0 pin: bit x at 0 powers the P0[x] output from the V30 rail (reset state), at 1 from the 1V8P rail.

fields.name: P1_OUT_CTRL
fields.text: One bit per P1 pin: bit x at 0 powers the P1[x] output from the V30 rail (reset state), at 1 from the 1V8P rail.

fields.name: DIVN_OUTPUT_EN
fields.text: 1 sends the DIVN clock out on its dedicated pin P0_15, which must be set up as a GPIO output.

fields.name: RC32M_OUTPUT_EN
fields.text: 1 sends the RC32M clock out on its dedicated pin P0_13, which must be set up as a GPIO output.

fields.name: XTAL32M_OUTPUT_EN
fields.text: 1 sends the XTAL32M clock out on its dedicated pin P0_12, which must be set up as a GPIO output.

fields.name: RCX_OUTPUT_EN
fields.text: 1 sends the RCX clock out on its dedicated pin P0_16, which must be set up as a GPIO output.

fields.name: RC32K_OUTPUT_EN
fields.text: 1 sends the RC32K clock out on its dedicated pin P0_17, which must be set up as a GPIO output.

fields.name: XTAL32K_OUTPUT_EN
fields.text: 1 sends the XTAL32K clock out on its dedicated pin P0_14, which must be set up as a GPIO output.

fields.name: FUNC_CLOCK_EN
fields.text: 1 routes the clock chosen by FUNC_CLOCK_SEL out to a pin.

fields.name: FUNC_CLOCK_SEL
fields.text: Clock put on the pin when PID is FUNC_CLOCK: 0x0 XTAL32K, 0x1 RC32K, 0x2 RCX, 0x3 XTAL32M, 0x4 RC32M, 0x5 DIVN, 0x6 and 0x7 reserved.

fields.name: P1_09_LOWDRV

fields.name: FRZ_CMAC_WDOG
fields.text: Write 1 to freeze the CMAC software watchdog timer; writing 0 has no effect.

fields.name: FRZ_SWTIM4
fields.text: Write 1 to freeze SW Timer4; writing 0 has no effect.

fields.name: FRZ_SWTIM3

fields.name: FRZ_SWTIM2

fields.name: FRZ_DMA

fields.name: FRZ_USB

fields.name: FRZ_SYS_WDOG
fields.text: Write 1 to freeze the SYS software watchdog timer; writing 0 has no effect. Works only while WATCHDOG_CTRL_REG.NMI_RST is 0.

fields.name: FRZ_RESERVED

fields.text: Write 1 to let the SYS software watchdog timer run again; writing 0 has no effect.
